plants.name: Banksia conferta var. conferta
plants.context: Banksia conferta var. conferta [Section 28] is a small tree with small flower-heads varying in shades from a pinkish-brown to lemon.

plants.name: Blandfordia grandiflora
plants.context: Time now to see, in the Sydney Flora area, Blandfordia grandiflora [Section 191] with large bell-like flowers of orange-red tipped yellow, known as the Christmas Bell.

title: In Flower This Week, 18.4.97
author: Barbara Daly
intro: Displayed with the Cape York Exhibition is the lovely Cape York Lily, Curcuma australasica, a member of the ginger family. The large, pleated leaves sheathe the clusters of rosy pink flowers which change to green on ageing. The tuberous stock was roasted and eaten by Aborigines.

plants.name: Curcuma australasica
plants.context: Displayed with the Cape York Exhibition is the lovely Cape York Lily, Curcuma australasica, a member of the ginger family.

plants.name: Crowea saligna
plants.context: Crowea saligna [Section 174] is yet a small plant well covered with thick, waxy pink star-like flowers.

plants.context: Opposite the rainforest of varying shades of green, find Correa `Canes Hybrid' [Section 124].

plants.name: Melaleuca thymifolia
plants.context: Nearby Melaleuca thymifolia [Section 124] displays the first of its fine, lacy flowers.

plants.context: Towards the Rockery area Callistemon `Glasshouse Country' [Section 110] is an open, graceful shrub with lovely pink bottlebrush flowers.

plants.context: There is much to see in the Rockery and worth finding is Prostanthera porcata [Section 15R] bearing soft pink bugle-shaped flowers on a fairly open shrub.

plants.context: Not so easy to find is a very small Verticordia blepharophylla [Section 15R] with feathery mauve flowers clinging to the stems.

plants.name: Diplopeltis huegelii
plants.context: Nearby is Diplopeltis huegelii [Section 15R] with low, spreading branches and pink flowers loosely arranged on upright stems.

plants.name: Acacia fauntleroyi
plants.context: Some wattles in flower include Acacia fauntleroyi [Section 3] with erect trunk well covered with attractive curly bark and on top, spreading branches bearing golden, fluffy flower balls.

plants.context: Acacia uncinata [Section 3] has deep yellow flower balls spaced along the low, arching branches.

plants.name: Acacia iteaphylla
plants.context: Acacia iteaphylla [Section 3] is a many- branched tall shrub bearing sprays of soft, lemon flower balls.

plants.name: Chloanthes parviflora
plants.context: Opposite the Nursery and worth finding is Chloanthes parviflora [Section 44] a low plant with wrinkly leaves concealing the lemon-throated tubular green flowers.

plants.name: Actinotus helianthi
plants.context: Much easier to see is Flannel Flower, Actinotus helianthi [Section 191], with large daisy-like flowers with soft, velvety petals.

title: In Flower This Week, 25.4.97
author: Barbara Daly
intro: The lovely Cape York Lily, Curcuma australasica, which is a member of the ginger family, stands supreme as part of the Cape York Exhibition in the Visitors Centre. This deciduous, tuberous plant has long, rippled, spade-like leaves which sheathe the clusters of rosy pink flowers. The flowers fade to green on ageing.

plants.name: Curcuma australasica
plants.context: The lovely Cape York Lily, Curcuma australasica, which is a member of the ginger family, stands supreme as part of the Cape York Exhibition in the Visitors Centre.

plants.context: Nearby, Dampiera stricta [Section 15F], jammed between the rocks, is showy with bright blue flowers on the tips of the upright stems.

plants.context: Compare its growth and flower colour with Dampiera subspicata [Section 15H], a paler shade of blue, and Dampiera diversifolia [Section 15H, 15L], a ground-hugging plant with darker flowers.

plants.context: And in all areas the brilliant yellow straw flowers of Bracteantha species [Section 15] and the mounding plants with soft foliage and small mauve daisy flowers of Brachyscome multifida [Section 15] are eyecatching.

plants.context: The colour of these plants, together with the white daisies of Olearia ramulosa [Section 15A] and the dense, prostrate Hibbertia serpyllifolia [Section 15A] dotted with small yellow flowers, are worth admiring.

plants.context: Walk around the tall many-stemmed shrub, Hakea petiolaris [Section 4] Sea-urchin Hakea.

plants.context: Chrysocephalum apiculatum [Section 15R] is an entanglement of low, green foliage well covered with clusters of heads of bright orange flowers.

plants.name: Correa pulchella 'Pink Mist'
plants.context: Correa pulchella `Pink Mist' [Section 15S] is a small, dainty shrub adorned with pink tubular flowers.

title: In Flower This Week, 22.5.98
author: Barbara Daly
intro: Canberra City is a blaze with the lovely autumn colours of exotic trees. The Botanic Gardens, however, has only native trees and very few of those lose their leaves in winter.

intro: This lovely autumn weather makes pleasurable walking where flowers, including wattles, banksias and others are so colourful. To start, view Acacia aphylla [Section 221] in a pot outside the Visitor Centre door. It resembles a skeletalised plant dotted with single yellow flower balls. The walk commences up above the Nursery to find Acacia jibberdingensis from a small WA town called Jibberding.

plants.name: Hakea corymbosa

plants.name: Dampiera lanceolata var. lanceolata
plants.context: Dampiera lanceolata var. lanceolata [Section 15R] is a low-growing dense, wiry herb beautified with deep blue flowers.

plants.name: Dampiera sericantha
plants.context: Compare it with Dampiera sericantha [Section 15R], nearby which is a neater, dwarf herb with flowers a lighter shade of blue.

plants.name: Lasiopetalum involucratum
plants.context: Lasiopetalum involucratum [Section 15R] is small and dense with cheery pink flowers amid many buds covered with rust coloured calyces.

plants.name: Hardenbergia violacea
plants.context: False sarsaparilla, Hardenbergia violacea [Section 15S] is upright and shrubby and bears many deep purple clusters of pea-shaped flowers.

plants.context: It harmonises well, here with Leucophyta brownii ‘Cape Le Grande’ [Section 15S] a fairly dense dwarf shrub with wiry silver-grey stems and minute silver-grey leaves.

plants.context: Opposite, Bossiaea walkeri [Section 211] is rather odd in appearance for this plant has flattened stems which helps the plant lose less water.

plants.name: Senecio lautus subsp. dissectifolius

plants.name: Phebalium glandulosum subsp. glandulosum
plants.context: Phebalium glandulosum subsp. glandulosum [Section 211] is an attractive small plant tipped with clusters of yellow flowers fluffy with long anthers.

plants.name: Hybanthus floribundus
plants.context: Hybanthus floribundus [Section 211] has, in profusion, tiny pale blue flowers arranged over this small shrub.

plants.name: Westringia crassifolia
plants.context: Westringia crassifolia [Section 211] bears mauve bugle-shaped flowers which beautify this woody, windswept plant.

plants.name: Pimelia linifolia subsp. linifolia
plants.context: Beside it is Pimelia linifolia subsp. linifolia [Section 211] which is quite compact and covered with clusters of tiny white flowers.

plants.name: Acacia granitica
plants.context: The medium erect tree bright with rods of bright yellow flowers is Acacia granitica [Section 211] while at its base Prostanthera aspalathoides [Section 211] bears small red tubular flowers on the small shrub.

plants.name: Prostanthera aspalathoides
plants.context: The medium erect tree bright with rods of bright yellow flowers is Acacia granitica [Section 211] while at its base Prostanthera aspalathoides [Section 211] bears small red tubular flowers on the small shrub.

plants.name: Eucalyptus caesia subsp. magna

plants.name: Hakea crassinervia
plants.context: See, also, Hakea crassinervia [Section 221] low and sprawling with lovely clusters of deep pink flowers along its extended branches.

title: In Flower This Week - 20.8.99
author: Naomi Bell
intro: As you walked up the ramp towards the Visitor Centre, on your left is Allocasuarina torulosa [Section 224]. This large tree has been covered in shiny, rusty-brown male flowers for quite a while now. Similarly, the Allocasuarina portuensis [Section 221] has also been covered in male flowers that give it a rusty shine for some months.

plants.name: Allocasuarina torulosa
plants.context: As you walked up the ramp towards the Visitor Centre, on your left is Allocasuarina torulosa [Section 224].

plants.name: Allocasuarina portuensis
plants.context: Similarly, the Allocasuarina portuensis [Section 221] has also been covered in male flowers that give it a rusty shine for some months.

plants.name: Templetonia retusa
plants.context: Templetonia retusa [Section 174] is a shrub, about a metre and a half in height, with large rusty-red pea flowers, while a little further on is Eutaxia obovata [Section 174] a lower-growing shrub with masses of tiny yellow and orange pea flowers.

plants.name: Eutaxia obovata

plants.name: Odixia angusta

plants.name: Acacia podalyriifolia

plants.name: Syzygium paniculatum
plants.context: Syzygium paniculatum [Section 124] is more a shrub than a tree with lots of magenta-coloured small fruits dotted over it.

plants.name: Westringia longifolia

plants.name: Acacia kettlewelliae
plants.context: Not quite out yet but looking attractive is Acacia kettlewelliae [Section 2], while Acacia saliciformis [Section 2] is in almost full flower with pale yellow balls and Acacia boormanii [Section 2] is covered in golden flower balls.

plants.name: Acacia saliciformis

plants.context: Acacia covenyi [Section 3] is a little further on, with grey-blue foliage and large, golden-yellow sprays of flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea aspleniifolia

plants.context: Further on, Hakea lissocarpha [Section 112] has a crown of cream flowers and its neighbour is a patch of Micromyrtus ciliata [Section 112] from just coming into bud to completely out.

title: In Flower This Week - 27.8.99
author: Naomi Bell
intro: Homoranthus papillatus [Section 222] is not yet in flower but is covered in attractive reddish flower buds which form a haze over the whole plant. plants.name: Grevillea diminuta

plants.name: Grevillea aspleniifolia

plants.name: Acacia podalyriifolia

title: In Flower This Week - 3.12.99
author: Barbara Daly
intro: This early summer's walk follows the Main Path where bottlebrushes and tea-trees are in flower. Notice first, outside the Visitor Centre doors in the colourful pots, the lovely Cyanostegia lanceolata bearing many soft mauve flowers. The walk then starts at the far end of the Café building.

title: In Flower This Week 12.1.2001
author: Barbara Daly
intro: The large pink trumpet flowers with maroon centres which can be seen over the top of the wall opposite the Visitor Centre are those of Pandorea jasminoides [Section 212]. Above, Alyogyne hakeifolia [Section 210] arches its branches supporting mauve, hibiscus-like flowers.

plants.name: Lophostemon confertus
plants.context: (Note that most banksia flower spikes are upright.) Also worth viewing is a Brush Box, Lophostemon confertus [Section 37], a tall, dense tree resplendent with large fine feathery flowers…another lovely.

title: In Flower This Week 19.1.2001

intro: Admire the lovely mottled red trunks and the clusters of fluffy white flowers of the Smooth-barked Apple, Angophora costata [Sections 168, 169], in the car park. In the moon-shaped garden, see the blue flowers of Dampiera sylvestris [Section 174] amid the entanglement of the silvery white branches of Leucophyta brownii 'Cape Le Grand' [Section 174].

plants.name: Templetonia retusa
plants.context: Follow the path past the Café to the last of the tables where there is a small triangular bed with Templetonia retusa [Section 244].

plants.name: Hardenbergia 'Mini Haha'
plants.context: Branch off to the right to see Hardenbergia ‘Mini Haha’ [Section 240], though there is nothing ‘mini’ about the area of ground this lovely scrambling blue flowering plant is covering.

plants.name: Acacia alata
plants.context: Acacia alata [Section 240], back on the Main Path, displays its fluffy cream balls of flowers on the ends of tiny stalks, but has lots of vicious looking spikes too.

plants.name: Westringia longifolia
plants.context: Westringia longifolia [Section 123a] has dainty mauve and white flowers with more mauve buds to open.

plants.name: Acacia boormanii
plants.context: Opposite is Acacia boormanii [Section 122] with reddish stems, green leaves and bright golden balls, a delight.

plants.name: Eriostemon myoporoides subs. myoporoides
plants.context: Immediately in front of it is Eriostemon myoporoides subs. myoporoides [Section 122], about a metre high, with white, star-like flowers and still just a few pink buds to open out.

plants.name: Acacia podalyriifolia
plants.context: Acacia podalyriifolia [Section 122] is another of the wattles with silver-grey foliage and whose flowers are golden balls.

plants.name: Eucalyptus pulverulenta
plants.context: Further on, Eucalyptus pulverulenta [Section 37] has its dainty flowers tucked into its leaves.

plants.name: Banksia speciosa
plants.context: Beside it is Banksia speciosa [Section 37], with long grey-green toothed leaves but only one prominent yellow-green cone in the forefront of the tree.

plants.name: Crowea 'Festival'
plants.context: Read the Root Rot sign and marvel at how well the mass plantings of Crowea ‘Festival’ [Section 123] brighten this area with their mauve flowers.

plants.name: Epacris calvertiana var. calvertiana
plants.context: On your way back down the hill find Epacris calvertiana var. calvertiana [Section 17], an upright shrub very well covered with small cream-white tubular flowers.

title: In Flower This Week 20.09.2002
author: Naomi Bell
intro: On leaving the Visitor Centre turn left and, a little way down, is Eremophila ‘Murchison Magic’ [Section 210], with very soft grey foliage and drooping orange flowers tucked between its leaves. There are a number of small plants in flower on either side of the walkway. Just past the small bridge, on the Rainforest side is Indigofera australis [Section 125], a very dainty plant with mauve-pink pea

plants.name: Grevillea 'Pink Pi
plants.context: Just about opposite is Grevillea ‘Pink Pixie’[Section 124], with typical spider-like flowers of a delicate pink.

plants.name: Grevillea 'White Wings'

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa var. spinulosa
plants.context: On the Brittle Gum Lawn is Banksia spinulosa var. spinulosa [Section 107], with orange cones that have dark red styles.

plants.name: Westringia glabra
plants.context: Walk across the lawn to the path, and continue on to Westringia glabra [Section 6], a medium sized shrub about half a metre high, with blue-mauve flowers scattered all over it.

plants.name: Hakea corymbosa
plants.context: Then on to see Hakea corymbosa [Section 20], a nicely shaped plant with rather stiff, sharp pointed leaves.

plants.name: Hakea purpurea
plants.context: Hakea purpurea [Section 20] has its red-purple flower clusters huddled between its leaves too.

plants.name: Hakea recurva
plants.context: Here also is Hakea recurva [Section 20], again with spikes on its leaves.

plants.name: Astartea sp
plants.context: One of these is Astartea sp.

plants.name: Baeckea virgata
plants.context: Baeckea virgata [Section 41] is a large bush with lots of spent, brown flower capsules, which at a quick glance, could be taken for flowers!

plants.name: Melaleuca nodosa
plants.context: Baeckea virgata [Section 41] is a large bush with lots of spent, brown flower capsules, which at a quick glance, could be taken for flowers! Melaleuca nodosa [Section 41] is a large shrub dotted all over with small, creamy-coloured flowers with a tiny brownish centre.

plants.name: Allocasuarina inophloia
plants.context: Allocasuarina inophloia [Section 40] (not in flower) has the shaggiest of bark all over its trunks looking rather like the coat of some animal.

plants.name: Allocasuarina torulosa
plants.context: Allocasuarina torulosa [Section 40] has a reddish-brown sheen of tiny flowers all over it.

plants.name: Hakea francisiana
plants.context: Hakea francisiana [Section 38] is a very large sprawling tree at the very top of which are a few flowers completely out.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia var. ericifolia
plants.context: Banksia ericifolia var. ericifolia [Section37] with rather large orange cones and its styles are the same colour.

plants.name: Acacia pravissima
plants.context: Acacia pravissima [Section 123b] has pendulous branches with tiny leaves where its clusters of yellow flowers sit comfortably.

title: In Flower This Week 27.09.2002
author: Naomi Bell
intro: Zieria prostrata - click for larger image

plants.name: Restio tetraphyllus
plants.context: In the garden just below the Visitor Centre is Restio tetraphyllus [Section 223], a grass-like plant with upright stems of a yellow-brown colour with what looks like plumes for flowers.

plants.name: Homoranthus sp
plants.context: Homoranthus sp.

plants.name: Eremophila nivea
plants.context: In contrast Eremophila nivea [Section 221] is an upright plant with silver-grey foliage and tubular mauve flowers contrasting well with its foliage.

plants.name: Zieria prostrata
plants.context: Zieria prostrata [Section 221] is a woody looking plant, covered all over with tiny pink flowers.

plants.name: Acacia 'Gold Lace'
plants.context: Acacia ‘Gold Lace’ [Section 170], just near the shelter at the bottom of the car park, is a sprawling, prostrate wattle complete, of course, with lots of golden balls.

plants.name: Eriostemon myoporoides subsp. myoporoides
plants.context: Eriostemon myoporoides subsp. myoporoides [Section 170] has pink buds opening out to white flowers with five petals and a little touch of orange in the middle.

plants.name: Ozothamnus expansifolius
plants.context: Almost opposite the board is a shrubby plant, Ozothamnus expansifolius [Section 232], with brownish buds and lots of cream daisy flowers.

plants.name: Philotheca difformis subsp. smithianus
plants.context: Along on the right is the small Philotheca difformis subsp. smithianus [Section 171], with tiny star-like flowers and lots of brown buds not open yet.

plants.name: Ranunculus collinus
plants.context: Ranunculus collinus [Section 171] is a native buttercup and makes an attractive ground cover plant, with each small stalk having three leaves and its bright yellow flowers held up above the leaves.

plants.name: Calothamnus quadrifidus
plants.context: Looking down across the Boundary Road, there are three Calothamnus quadrifidus [Section 99].

plants.name: Epacris gunnii
plants.context: Epacris gunnii [Section 232] is a small, upright heath with white flowers from about two thirds of the way up its stems.

plants.name: Eucalyptus barberi
plants.context: Eucalyptus barberi [Section 232] is more a mallee than a tree, with its flowers nestling amongst its leaves.

plants.name: Spyridium obcordatum
plants.context: There is a small paved area leading back into the inner garden, where Spyridium obcordatum [Section 232] shows off tiny white to cream flowers.

plants.name: Phebalium squameum subsp. retusum
plants.context: Phebalium squameum subsp. retusum [Section 232] is also covered in tiny, fluffy white flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea australis
plants.context: Grevillea australis [Section 232], is a rather sprawling plant compared to the size of its tiny leaves, with flowers of creamy white which must produce lots of nectar as the bees are crawling all over it.

plants.name: Ozothamnus ledifolius
plants.context: Compare Ozothamnus expansifolius [Section 231], a small pine-like plant covered in brown buds with just a few cream flowers, with Ozothamnus ledifolius [Section 231], a small bright green plant with just a few tiny yellow flowers at the end of its branches.

plants.name: Westringia rubiifolia
plants.context: Westringia rubiifolia [Section 236] has its tiny white flowers sitting in a ring of leaves at the tip of each branch.

plants.name: Leptospermum myrsinoides

plants.context: Grevillea acanthifolia [Section 303] is another grey foliage plant with lots of pink-mauve toothbrush flowers and more buds yet to open.

plants.name: Grevillea flexuosa

plants.name: Boronia pinnata

plants.name: Allocasuarina nana
plants.context: A group planting of Allocasuarina nana [Section 191h] has the ends of their branches covered with the bronze-red shine of their tiny male flowers.

plants.name: Boronia deanei
plants.context: Boronia deanei [Section 191e] displays tiny pink flowers and numerous, equally tiny, dark pink buds.

plants.name: Eutaxia obovata
plants.context: A group planting of Eutaxia obovata [Section 19] has tiny orange and red pea flowers up the stems and, just behind them, Hovea acutifolia [Section 19], another pea, has almost purple flowers.

plants.name: Hovea acutifolia
plants.context: A group planting of Eutaxia obovata [Section 19] has tiny orange and red pea flowers up the stems and, just behind them, Hovea acutifolia [Section 19], another pea, has almost purple flowers.

plants.name: Hakea purpurea
plants.context: A group of Hakea purpurea [Section 20], a medium sized, upright plant, have open branches and bright red-maroon flowers up the stems.

plants.name: Zieria prostrata
plants.context: Past the Rock Garden, on the left, is Zieria prostrata [Section 110] covering a large area with its tiny pink flowers scattered over a prostrate plant.

plants.context: Nearby Eriostemon australasius [Section 221] displays its lovely pink star flowers on an open shrub.

plants.name: Olearia phlogopappa
plants.context: Olearia phlogopappa [Section 5] is an upright shrub displaying white daisies.

plants.name: Pultenaea foliolosa

plants.name: Prostanthera phylicifolia

plants.context: Close by, Telopea ‘Doug’s Hybrid’ [Section 30] is well covered with waratahs, still to mature to brilliant red flowers.

plants.context: Opposite, Grevillea acanthifolia [Section 30] is low with pink toothbrush-like flowers on long lateral branches.

plants.name: Micromyrtus ciliata
plants.context: Micromyrtus ciliata [Section 10] borders the path, its low lateral branches coloured with flowers, white and red according to age.

title: In Flower This Week 10.10.2003
intro: If you’ve overdosed on colour at Floriade this spring you’ll be ready for a wander through the wild beauty of Australian native plants here at the Gardens. Don’t put your camera away though. If you “get up close and personal” with the exquisite flowers you will be rewarded with some great macro shots.

plants.name: Hibbertia empetrifolia

plants.name: Verticordia pennigera

plants.name: Actinotus helianthi

plants.name: Ceratopetalum gummiferum
plants.context: Even if you saw nothing else, just come to the Gardens to behold the spectacle of the gorgeous New South Wales Christmas Bush, Ceratopetalum gummiferum [Section 142], on the left hand side of the entrance to the Tasmanian Garden!

plants.name: Anigozanthos
plants.context: Starting with the patch of Western Australian Kangaroo Paws, Anigozanthos flavidus [Section 171] on the opposite side of that path, observe the colour variations of this plant throughout the Gardens as you wander and pass numerous clumps on your way to the waterfall in the Rockery [Section 15].

plants.name: Eucalyptus extrica

plants.name: Xanthorrhoea macronema
plants.context: On the way back down on your left, Xanthorrhoea macronema [Section 15D], trunkless and displaying an unusual almost banksia-like flower spear, is more than subtly different from the other grass trees.

plants.name: Podacarpus elatus
plants.context: Back on the Main Path into the Conifer Section, notice on your left the fresh crop of seeds, on plum-like fleshy stems, appearing on the Plum Pine, Podacarpus elatus [Section 110].

plants.name: Banksia aemulata
plants.context: The Wallum Banksia, Banksia aemulata [Section 16], a little further along on the right, now has a bush-load of fresh cream (tinged pale lime) flower cones at all stages of maturation amongst its previous years’ brushes with their big woody follicles.

plants.name: Persoonia pinifolia
plants.context: Further along on the left is a very happy Geebung, Persoonia pinifolia [Section 110], lit up by its terminal spikes of yellow flowers, looking like bunches of grapes when its fruit sets.

plants.name: Athrotaxis laxifolia
plants.context: Opposite it, to the left of the entrance to the Conifer Loop, Athrotaxis laxifolia [Section 80], a pencil-pine-like conifer from Tasmania, is sprouting small spherical cones, like baubles.

plants.name: Backhousia citriodora
plants.context: Continuing along the Main Path, at the end of this section on the right hand side, find Backhousia citriodora [Section 80], the very fragrant Lemon Myrtle, punching out its furry little fistfuls of white flowers.

plants.name: Alocasia macrorrhizos
plants.context: As you enter the Rainforest, Alocasia macrorrhizos [Section 114], huge leaves catching the sun on your left, now has spathe-like green/white flowers emerging, the rod (spadix) inside turning from green/cream to bright orange and brown.

plants.name: Ceratopetalum apetalum
plants.context: High above you the two Coachwoods, Ceratopetalum apetalum [Section 146] are fully out in flower, as are the very tall Wattles, Acacia elata [Section 146] behind it.

plants.name: Acacia elata

plants.name: Lepidozamia peroffskyana
plants.context: Continue along the Main Path, passing Burrawangs, Lepidozamia peroffskyana [Section 146, 160] both on the left and right, about to fan out their new set of leaves.

plants.name: Correa glabra
plants.context: On the right several Correa glabra (green flowered form)[Section 212] plants look like they’ve been decorated with glow-in-the-dark little lanterns.

plants.name: Poa labillardieri
plants.context: Now intimately acquainted with this Grass Tree, you will recognize that the many species from other regions throughout these Gardens are all a little different from each other! Curving back downhill, on the left, the seed heads of Poa labillardieri [Section 175], spray out of the earth in firework fashion.

plants.name: Pelargonium rodneyanum
plants.context: That’s Pelargonium rodneyanum [Section 223] on your right above the wall; Australia’s most beautiful geranium, the loveliest magenta colour.

plants.name: Grevillea lanigera
plants.context: And the very compact Grevillea lanigera [Section 223], succulent-like in appearance, its pale yellow/soft pink curvy flower clusters looking like they want to escape.

plants.name: Crowea 'Festival'
plants.context: As you come around the bend to your right there is a small shrub with spray like foliage and deep pink five petaled star-like flowers with white centres, Crowea ‘Festival’ [Section 224].

plants.name: Eremophila
plants.context: As you are about to turn right, there is a small bush with complex branches near the sprinkler, Eremophila divaricata [Section 211], with stalkless soft mauve tubular flowers.

plants.name: Eucalyptus nortonii
plants.context: Standing guard at the entrance is the first of several multi-trunked Mallee Gums, Eucalyptus nortonii [Section 211], full of promise, showing you at eye-level Eucalyptus flower buds, little caps tightly glued on, simply falling off when released when the flower is ready to be pollinated.

plants.name: Melaleuca lanceolata subsp. lanceolata
plants.context: About halfway along this path, on the right, is a chunky dense tree, Melaleuca lanceolata subsp. lanceolata [Section 211], its small white flower brushes obviously a five star insect haven, all flat out pollinating and mating.

plants.name: Callistemon brachyandrus
plants.context: Beyond the Mallee Fowl is Callistemon brachyandrus [Section 211], with its golden orange bottlebrushes.

plants.name: Chrysocephalum apiculatum
plants.context: A few paces further along the path is Chrysocephalum apiculatum [Section 211], very fine almost fern-like foliage, stipped at the ends with very bright yellow dots.

plants.name: Senna artemisioides
plants.context: At the T-junction Senna artemisioides [Section 211] has begun to adorn its lovely rounded soft green shape with its yellow buttercup-like flowers.

title: In Flower This Week 20.02.2004
intro: As you emerge mid-section from the sheltered spaciousness of the Eucalypt Lawn [Sections 34, 35], perhaps after a Summer Jazz Concert and/or picnic, and leave the colourful trunks of some 80 of the 800 or so Australian iconic gum trees behind, see the dead-looking unnamed wattle tree [Section 3] on your right at the edge of the lawn, curiously springing back to life - a wreath of re-growth around

plants.name: Acacia oshanesii
plants.context: Not many identical twins among them, although as seedlings they all start with similar feathery leaves like Acacia oshanesii [Section 3], which you just passed on your right, its ‘highliter yellow’ flower balls dancing on its very dark green fernlike foliage.

plants.name: Acacia subulata
plants.context: Turn left to see on your left Acacia subulata [Section 19], which has flattened leaf stalks (phyllodes) instead of leaves and soft yellow flower balls in bunches along its leggy stems.

plants.name: Acacia fulva
plants.context: A little further on is a stand of tall Acacia fulva [Section 19], which has retained its very lovely soft feathery mid-green leaves and has tightly packed rods of yellow flower balls sticking out of its foliage mass.

plants.name: Acacia melanoxylon
plants.context: There is a very large Blackwood, Acacia melanoxylon [Section 20], a little off the path on your left, full of cream-coloured flower balls.

plants.name: Chrysocephalum apiculatum
plants.context: Continue and at the end of the lawn on your left, in a bed edged with dark yellow Chrysocephalum apiculatum green leaf form [Section 4] and vivid yellow straw flowers, stands Angophora melanoxylon [Section 4] with bunches of white furry flowers, almost a eucalypt.

plants.name: Angophora melanoxylon
plants.context: Continue and at the end of the lawn on your left, in a bed edged with dark yellow Chrysocephalum apiculatum green leaf form [Section 4] and vivid yellow straw flowers, stands Angophora melanoxylon [Section 4] with bunches of white furry flowers, almost a eucalypt.

plants.name: Callistemon pachyphyllus 'Smoked Salmon'
plants.context: Then turn left down the hill, noticing Callistemon pachyphyllus ‘Smoked Salmon’ [Section 110] on your right, an unusual smoked salmon coloured bottlebrush.

plants.name: Smoked Salmon'
plants.context: Then turn left down the hill, noticing Callistemon pachyphyllus ‘Smoked Salmon’ [Section 110] on your right, an unusual smoked salmon coloured bottlebrush.

plants.name: Pandorea pandorana
plants.context: A little further on your right the Wonga Wonga Vine Pandorea pandorana [Section 110] hangs very heavy with its long seed pods which have started to curl open to release furry floating seeds.

plants.name: Eremophila longifolia
plants.context: Just past the next turn-off on your left is Eremophila longifolia [Section 7], looking like a little weeping willow with pink tubular flowers.

plants.name: Callistemon chisholmii
plants.context: Turn left through the bollards (just past the toilet block) to admire Callistemon chisholmii [Section 10], a tall, weepy but shapely shrub, its leaves a calming green backdrop for its pleasant cream, as well as soft pink, brushes.

plants.name: Callistemon citrinus
plants.context: Looking over your left shoulder you’ll see several tree-like lemon-scented Crimson Bottlebrushes, Callistemon citrinus [Section 9], part of a vast foliage collage into the distance, a really pretty picture.

plants.name: Eucalyptus deuaensis
plants.context: Turn down the pebblecrete Main Path and a little further along look up to see both Eucalyptus deuaensis [Section 10], right, so similar to the Angophora we saw earlier except for its gum-nuts, and the blushing brushes of the River Bottlebrush, Callistemon sieberi [Section 11], left, meeting above the path.

plants.name: Callistemon sieberi

plants.name: Leptospermum petersonii
plants.context: Continue, some more Callistemon chisholmii left and right [Section 10, 11] and before the intersection, on your left, is a tall, multi-stemmed tea tree, Leptospermum petersonii [Section 12] with very fragrant dark green leaves and white tea tree flowers.

plants.name: Callistemon viminalis
plants.context: Across the road are some large Callistemon viminalis [Section 143], weeping their bright red bottlebrushes.

plants.name: Macrozamia moorei
plants.context: A colony of recently transplanted rare 400-year-old native cycads, Macrozamia moorei, and several large native palms now graces the Entrance to the Australian National Botanic Gardens, a front yard blitz financed with funds raised by the Friends of the Gardens’ Summer Concert Series.

title: In Flower This Week 27.02.2004

The longer you stay, the more you see! Even the rock in front of you has an interesting beauty in its colourful facets, which adds to the wonder of the three-dimensional interplay of foliage-tones and -textures. Stay long enough to let an Easter

plants.name: Grevillea 'Mason's Hybrid'

plants.name: Homoranthus darwinioides
plants.context: So, the variety of foliage of these plants is now very obviously a focus! Homoranthus darwinioides [Section 15F] has fully grown and its quaint pairs of light yellow flowers sit prettily atop the rounded grey-green bush, whose tiny leaves have a perplexing fruity fragrance.

plants.name: Leptosema aphyllum
plants.context: Leptosema aphyllum [Section 14] not bothering with any leaves at all, has flattened stems and gets by nicely in this unusual fashion, although it looks a little awkward, if not absurd!

plants.name: Muehlenbeckia axillaris
plants.context: Muehlenbeckia axillaris [Section 15T] spills and spreads in comfort, tiny leaves, tiny flowers, like a big puddle.

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia var. integrifolia
plants.context: Several Banksia integrifolia var. integrifolia [Sections 15L, 15C] are the prostrate form of the Coast Banksia and are forming their new creamy flower cones already.

plants.name: Cladium procerum
plants.context: The Leafy Twig Rush, Cladium procerum [Section 15Q] with its brown heads now forming seeds.

plants.name: Lythrum salicaria
plants.context: The tall mauve flowered Lythrum salicaria [Section 15Q], now with only a few flowers left on its long spikes is a cosmopolitan species with some questioning whether it is truly ‘native’.

plants.name: Marsilea drummondii
plants.context: There’s also the strange 4-leaved-clover fern, Nardoo, Marsilea drummondii [Section 15Q] which can grow with floating leaves or as a land plant (see it near the tap) – its hidden spore capsules sustained the explorers Burke & Wills for a short time before their eventual death at Cooper’s Creek in 1861.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.context: The Australian Golden Wattle, Acacia pycnantha [Section 223] seen in front of the Visitors Centre, is now revealing its lovely fluffy golden clusters of flower balls.

plants.name: Eremophila bowmanii var.bowmanii
plants.context: So, starting in front of the waterfall in front of which emu bush, Eremophila bowmanii var.bowmanii [Section 15V] is a small open shrub where purple bugle flowers mix with their grey-green foliage and behind the notice board a pea-flower, Daviesia physodes [Section 15D] is a small shrub enveloped with black centred burnt orange pea shaped flowers.

plants.name: Leucopogon microphyllus
plants.context: Now, moving in an anti-clockwise direction where Leucopogon microphyllus [Section 15C] is so small with a covering of tiny white flowers mix with the dark foliage.

plants.name: Tetratheca bauerifolia
plants.context: Tetratheca bauerifolia [Section 15C] is also small and upright with small pink flowers.

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia
plants.context: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia [Section 15C] is a semi-prostrate plant with silver-backed leaves and still many lemon upright cylindrical flower spikes, spread across the path.

plants.name: Banksia 'Honeypots'
plants.context: Behind the large shrub opposite is Banksia ‘Honeypots’ [Section 15D] which displays its lovely yellow flower spikes with red styles over the upright plant.

plants.name: Gastrolobium rotundifolium
plants.context: Gastrolobium rotundifolium [Section 15E] also has pea-shaped flowers coloured orange with red centre.

plants.name: Eremophila maculata var.brevifolia
plants.context: In the centre of the next section emu bush Eremophila maculata var.brevifolia [Section 15F] has a covering of magenta coloured tubular flowers on an upright plant and Hypocalymma xanthopetalum [Section 15F] is yellow with small fluffy flowers on a low shrub hugging a rock face.

plants.name: Hypocalymma xanthopetalum

plants.name: Leucochrysum albicans subsp.albicans

plants.name: Micromyrtus ciliata

plants.name: Grevillea lanigera
plants.context: A ground cover, Grevillea lanigera [Section 15W] cascades down the slope, clad with red spider-like flowers mixes with Acacia pravissima ‘Kuranga Cascade’ [Section15 W], also a groundcover, clad with its golden flower balls.

plants.name: Acacia pravissima 'Kuranga Cascade'

plants.name: Hibbertia empetrifolia
plants.context: Up the stairs with a brilliant vista of yellow wattles, and edging the road, Hibbertia empetrifolia [Section 15H] is a dense entanglement of trailing stems showing the first of its many yellow flowers.

plants.name: Philotheca sp
plants.context: Philotheca sp. [Section 15H] is profusely clad with white star flower over the rounded shrub while Olearia astroloba [Section 15H] is attractive with mauve daisies which brightens the dark foliage.

plants.name: Olearia astroloba

plants.name: Richinocarpos bowmanii
plants.context: Down the path between the grass trees, Xanthorrhoea johnsonii [Section 15J.14] where Richinocarpos bowmanii [Section 15R] has many pink centred white flowers with down-turned petals over a neat shrub.

plants.name: Bulbine sp
plants.context: Down this path are a few Bulbine sp.

plants.name: Hardenbergia 'Mini-haha'
plants.context: Hardenbergia ‘Mini-haha’ [Section 15 S] is a pretty sight with large clusters of purple pea-flowers cling to the vine as it falls down the rock wall (these plants are seen throughout the Gardens).

plants.name: Acacia acinacea
plants.context: At the base Acacia acinacea [Section 15R] has long arching branches enveloped with yellow buds just exploding to small yellow flower balls.

plants.name: Craspedia jamesii
plants.context: Tufted herb, Billy-Buttons Craspedia jamesii [Section 15Q] grows its globular flower heads on bare upright stems surrounded by its silver-grey foliage.

plants.context: Continue along this road where a shrub Pomaderris velutina [Section31] is clad, in profusion with dense clusters of yellow flowers… quite spectacular!

plants.name: Prostanthera denticulata

plants.name: Pandorea pandorana

plants.name: Grevillea 'Wakiti Gem'

plants.name: Westringia longifolia

plants.name: Oxylobium ellipticum

plants.context: Along this road the Pale Vanilla lily, Arthropodium milleflorum [Section 15h] has long graceful flower spikes bearing small pale white-petalled flowers with iris-like leaves.

title: In Flower This Week 29.01.2010
author: Barbara Daly
intro: Beside the Visitors Information Centre doors, Australia’s Rhododendron lochiae with its red bell shaped flowers is something to see. This walk, however, is following the Main Path commencing at the far end of the café building. This path wanders through areas of the lovely gum trees with white trunks, the Sydney Basin flora, the Rock Garden and the cool Rainforest with flowers to enjoy on the way.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: So much of the Gardens are ‘In Flower This Week’! This weeks’ walk takes you around the Main Path loop. Allow 45 minutes. Begin at the Visitor Centre with a look at the stunning Orchid Display. These specimens are constantly updated, thus providing an ever-changing array of intricate flowers and scents.

plants.name: Boronia megastigma
plants.context: Take a moment here and smell the heavenly brown Boronia, Boronia megastigma[Section 174] …actually not everyone can detect its sweet perfume…don’t worry if you cannot, there are more scented flowers ahead!

plants.name: Acacia cognata "Green Mist"
plants.context: Turn left at the grey signpost by the puffy cushion-like green and yellow wattle Acacia cognata “Green Mist” [Section 210].

plants.name: Wollemia nobilis
plants.context: Further along on the right, stop to admire the beautiful cone-filled Wollemi Pine, Wollemia nobilis [Section 110].

plants.name: Banksia aemula
plants.context: A magnificent mature specimen of Banksia aemula (Wallum Banksia) [Section 15c] is interesting with fresh creamy-green flower spikes as well as different stages of fruiting cones, some with velvety seed pods showing, others dry and hard.

plants.name: Grevillea lanigera
plants.context: At the edge of the Rockery is the attractive low growing Grevillea lanigera [Section 15c] with nectar rich pink and cream flowers.

plants.name: Rhodanthe anthemoides
plants.context: Spilling out of the rock crevices near the waterfall is the beautiful yellow and white everlastings Rhodanthe anthemoides [Section 15v].

plants.name: Kennedia coccinea
plants.context: For all those brown Boronia fans, another chance to enjoy its perfume whilst looking at the colourful trailing vine Kennedia coccinea [Section 15s] with its striking mix of pink and orange petals.

plants.name: Acacia acinacea
plants.context: Continuing along the Main Path, Acacia acinacea [Section 15r] is a lovely combination of fine green foliage and the typical yellow fluffy flowers.

plants.name: Indigofera australis
plants.context: On the right side of the track, Indigofera australis [Section 4] is stunning with plenty of pink/purple flower stalks and rather sparse deep green/grey foliage.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima "Wirrimbirra White"
plants.context: As you reach the lawn, look back towards the waterfall and see if you can spot the white Waratah, Telopea speciosissima “Wirrimbirra White”[Section 15r], an amazing contrast to the more usual red Waratah.

plants.name: Helichrysum elatus
plants.context: Retrace your steps and continue along the Main Path in search of the beautiful soft and crinkly Helichrysum elatus [Section 18] with its large white and yellow dry papery flower heads and soft silver-grey hairy leaves.

plants.name: Telopea specisissima × oreades
plants.context: Onwards to the Sydney Region Gully where you will be greeted by some lovely, newly planted specimens of Telopea specisissima x oreades [Section 191].

plants.name: Grevillea sp
plants.context: It was a full house in the Grevillea sp [Section 191m] with three Eastern Spinebills all feeding on the numerous pink and red nectar-rich flowers on this mature shrub.

plants.name: Logania albifolia
plants.context: Just a little further along the track, enjoy the sweet scent within the dainty white flowers of Logania albifolia [Section 191d].

plants.name: Solanum brownii
plants.context: While having a look at the sandstone fossil, check out the attractive silk-like purple and yellow flowers of Solanum brownii [Section191l].

plants.name: Phebalium squamulosum subsp. lineare
plants.context: It’s hard to ignore the striking yellow flowers of Phebalium squamulosum subsp. lineare [Section 191h].

plants.name: Grevillea ripicola
plants.context: Check out the elaborate red, orange and yellow spidery flowers of Grevillea ripicola [Section 24].

plants.name: Isopogon anemonifolius
plants.context: The final plant is Isopogon anemonifolius [Section 26] with its beautifully decorative cones, yellow flowers and branched foliage.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: All the flowers described in this weeks’ “In Flower This Week” walk are located in the Rock Garden which is located about halfway along the Main Path loop trail. Please note this walk will involve steps.

plants.name: Wollemia nobilis
plants.context: As you leave the Rainforest, it is well worth stopping to admire the Wollemi Pine, Wollemia nobilis [Section 110] currently covered with numerous pollen-filled male cones and a single spiky female cone located at the back of the tree.

plants.name: Grevillea lanigera
plants.context: Grevillea lanigera [Section 15c] is an attractive, low growing plant filled with red/cream nectar rich flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Poorinda Royal Mantle'
plants.context: As you head up the steps it’s hard to miss the amazing spreading carpet of red hooked flowers of Grevillea ‘Poorinda Royal Mantle’ [Section 15d] ….certainly a favourite of the bees!

plants.name: Epacris breviflora
plants.context: A little further along is the beautiful upright Drumstick Heath or Epacris breviflora [Section 15b] with its snowy white flowers packed tightly along its prickly foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea aquifolium
plants.context: Just behind is the Grevillea aquifolium [Section 15b] or Holly Grevillea, with many yellow spider flowers opening to a warm pink/red colour.

plants.name: Homoranthus darwinioides
plants.context: Homoranthus darwinioides [Section 15f] has rather discreet pretty yellow and pink hanging flowers.

plants.name: Platytheca galioides
plants.context: Nearby is the stunning violet/purple flowers of Platytheca galioides [Section 15f] .

plants.name: Allocasuarina grampiana
plants.context: The beautiful Allocasuarina grampiana [Section 15b] is covered with red fluffy flower clusters on short stems along with many roundish, grey fruiting cones dotted among the lower branches.

plants.name: Homoranthus biflorus
plants.context: If you can smell a sweet honey-like scent while standing here, it’s probably the bee-covered Homoranthus biflorus [Section 15a] with its yellow nectar-rich flowers presented in flattish horizontal layers on the bush.

plants.name: Micromyrtus ciliata
plants.context: Taking the gravel path you will soon reach the stunning pink bush Micromyrtus ciliata [Section 15g] with its tiny feather-like lime green foliage and pink, soon-to-be white when open, flowers.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima 'Corroboree'
plants.context: The red waratah Telopea speciosissima ‘Corroboree’ [Section 15j] is stunning with its intricate red/crimson flowers.

plants.name: Darwinia masonii
plants.context: The dainty round bell shaped flowers of Darwinia masonii [Section 15j] are a beautiful combination of orange, yellow and cream and quite stylish and unusual when viewed closely.

plants.name: Conostylis aculeata
plants.context: Right next door, Conostylis aculeata [Section 15j] boasts velvety soft yellow flowers on velvety stems.

plants.name: Calytrix leschenaultii
plants.context: Heading back down towards the waterfall make a beeline for the purple pot filled with its matching mauve Calytrix leschenaultii [Section 15r].

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima 'Wirrimbirra White'
plants.context: A little further on is the amazing white waratah Telopea speciosissima ‘Wirrimbirra White’[Section 15r] with its huge white flowers and shapely seed pods.

plants.name: Hibbertia stellaris
plants.context: Just in front is the bright orange/yellow flowers of Hibbertia stellaris [Section 15r].

plants.name: Rhodanthe anthemoides
plants.context: Closer to the waterfall we can see the paperdaisy Rhodanthe anthemoides [Section 15s] spilling over the rocks.

plants.name: Boronia megastigma
plants.context: By now you might be able to smell the heavenly scent of the brown boronia Boronia megastigma [Section 15s] as you take the steps back down to the Main Path.

intro: Springtime flowers, especially along Banks Walk are so colourful as are the orchids inside the Visitors Information Centre. However those further afield are a joy to view. They include boronias coloured white, all shades of pink to red. To arrive there, select any path or follow that marked on the reverse map, to the section between 45 and 49.

plants.name: Hibbertia serpyllifolia
plants.context: In a clockwise direction, at the base of the stairs, Hibbertia serpyllifolia [Section 15c] is a small dense shrub clad with many smaller yellow flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Poorinda Royal Mantle'
plants.context: Opposite Grevillea ‘Poorinda Royal Mantle’ [Section 15d] is a dense ground cover with deep red toothbrush shaped flower spikes, which cascades down the rocks to the pools below.

plants.name: Brachyscome multifida
plants.context: Seen between the rocks edging the path Brachyscome multifida [Section 15d] are small plants clad with pink daily like flowers.

plants.name: Platytheca galioides
plants.context: Platytheca galioides [Section 15d] is a small open shrub bearing deep blue flowers.

plants.name: Hypocalymma xanthopetalum
plants.context: In another section Hypocalymma xanthopetalum [Section 15f] has tiny feathery flowers along its branches, seen between rocks.

plants.name: Plectranthus graveolens
plants.context: At the foot of the stairs, Plectranthus graveolens [Section 15a] is a herbaceous plant with large felt-like leaves and prominent spikes of pale blue flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Mason's Hybrid'
plants.context: Edging the stairs Grevillea ‘Mason’s Hybrid’ [Section 15h] is an ageing spreading shrub displaying many terminal pink-cream flower spikes.

plants.name: Grevillea lanigera
plants.context: At the top corner Grevillea lanigera [Section 15h] is a dense spreading groundcover clad with pink-cream spider-like flowers.

plants.name: Scaevola albida var. albida
plants.context: Edging this road Scaevola albida var. albida [Section 15h] is a semi-prostrate plant clad with both mauve and white fan-shaped flowers.

plants.name: Dampiera sylvestris
plants.context: There, too is Dampiera sylvestris [Section 15h], a suckering plant with blue flowers, seen above other plants.

plants.name: Thomasia petalocalyx
plants.context: Close-by Thomasia petalocalyx [Section 15h] is a dense shrub of medium size clad with small downturned pink cup-shaped flowers.

plants.name: Calothamnus tuberosus
plants.context: Beside this small path Calothamnus tuberosus [Section 14] is of medium size with pine-like foliage and with vivid red flower clusters which encircle the stems.

plants.name: Hibbertia vestita
plants.context: Hibbertia vestita [Section 15k] also has a coverage of small yellow flowers over the dense shrub while opposite

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia
plants.context: Banksia integrifolia [Section 15l] edging the path is dense and revealing many juvenile green-lemon flower spikes on this large hedge.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Birthday Candles'
plants.context: At the end of this path Banksia spinulosa ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 15l] is a dense dwarf shrub bearing many cream flower spikes.

plants.name: Acacia aneura var. aneura
plants.context: Close by a wattle, Acacia aneura var. aneura [Section 15l] a shrub of medium size interesting with short yellow flower rods.

plants.name: Verticordia pennigera
plants.context: In a pot, Verticordia pennigera [Section 15r] has small brilliant pink feathery flowers over the low spreading plant.

plants.name: Eremophila bignoniiflora × polyclada
plants.context: Continuing downwards, an emu-bush, Eremophila bignoniiflora x polyclada [Section 15r] an open, spreading shrub attractive with large open white bugle shaped flowers with dark spotted throat.

plants.name: Goodenia macmillanii
plants.context: Around the left corner Goodenia macmillanii [Section 15r], a low open spreading plant bearing soft pink flowers.

plants.name: Lythrum salicaria
plants.context: In front of the picturesque waterfall, growing between the rocks, Lythrum salicaria [Section 15q] is a tall plant bearing pink flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Grey clouds yesterday, sunshine today, what will tomorrow bring? Regardless this walk follows the Main Path and is always a pleasure so come and enjoy it. Many banksias are in bud as are other plants and only a few can be mentioned. The walk commences at the far end of the cafe building.

plants.name: Callistemon viminalis
plants.context: A large bottlebrush, Callistemon viminalis [Section 310] with red bottlebrush-like flowers dangle from the arching branches and the trunk clad with deep indented bark.

plants.name: Thryptomene sp
plants.context: Following the main path Thryptomene sp.

plants.name: Callistemon chisholmii
plants.context: At the cross-roads Callistemon chisholmii [Section 10] is tall and attractive with an overhead coverage of small pale pink bottlebrushes.

plants.name: Grevillea phanerophlebia
plants.context: Later, the sweetly scented perfume is from the large dense shrub, Grevillea phanerophlebia [Section 30] clad with dainty white flowers

plants.name: Banksia 'Birthday Candles'
plants.context: Almost opposite Banksia ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 30] is a dwarf spreading shrub profuse with pencil-like buds and now with mature gold flower spikes.

plants.name: Banksia pilostylis
plants.context: Behind a notice board Banksia pilostylis [Section25] has yellow flower spikes over the rounded shrub.

plants.name: Grevillea 'LadyO'
plants.context: At the next intersection Grevillea ‘LadyO’ [Section 26] is brilliant with fiery red spider-like flowers dangling from the low lateral branches.

plants.name: Persoonia acerosa
plants.context: A geebung, Persoonia acerosa [Section 26] is a low spreading shrub yellow with small tubular flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea dielsiana
plants.context: Grevillea dielsiana [Section 26] has orange-red flower clusters dangling among its fine foliage.

plants.name: Crowea exalata
plants.context: At the next intersection Crowea exalata [Section 112] has pink star-shaped flowers over the small shrub

plants.name: Correa 'Canberra Bells'
plants.context: While at the far end of this path Correa ‘Canberra Bells’ [Section 112] shows off its brilliant bell shaped flowers coloured dusky red and cream.

plants.name: Scaevola albida
plants.context: At the turn-off to the hothouse Scaevola albida [Section 191j] is a low spreading plant profuse with small pink fan- shaped flowers.

plants.name: Melaleuca thymifolia
plants.context: Melaleuca thymifolia [Section 191e] displays is small rounded curly mauve-pink flowers among other shrubs

plants.name: Hibbertia pedunculata
plants.context: In the Display garden, Hibbertia pedunculata [Section 191u] is a dense groundcover spotted with its bright yellow open flowers.

plants.name: Actinotus helianthi
plants.context: Close by is the renowned flannel flower, Actinotus helianthi [Section 191u,191l] with velvety grey foliage and soft white flowers on upright stems.

plants.name: Crowea saligna
plants.context: Behind the arched seat Crowea saligna [Section 191u] is so attractive with waxy deep pink flowers over the low spreading shrub.

plants.name: Scaevola ramosissima
plants.context: Towards the exit to this section Scaevola ramosissima [Section 191l] creeps about the rocks with purple fan shaped flowers along the small vines.

plants.name: Banksia aemula
plants.context: Pass by the rock pool, with water dragons, and waterfall, continuing past the large Banksia aemula [Section 15c] bright with cream flower spikes.

plants.name: Backhousia citriodora
plants.context: View, at the crossroad, Backhousia citriodora [Section 78] a neat tall shrub with clusters of cream fluffy flower clusters.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Tis a short walk with many flowers of differing shapes and sizes, many of which can be grown in home gardens. Almost opposite the doors of the Visitor Centre, Scaevola calliptera dangles its stems with deep purple fan shaped flowers over the edge of the pot.

plants.name: Scaevola calliptera
plants.context: Almost opposite the doors of the Visitor Centre, Scaevola calliptera dangles its stems with deep purple fan shaped flowers over the edge of the pot.

plants.name: Scaevola aemula 'Aussie Crawl'
plants.context: While almost opposite Scaevola aemula ‘Aussie Crawl’ [Section 174], creeps along the ground also attractive with paler purple flowers.

plants.name: Epacris impressa
plants.context: Edging the Banks Walk seen also the Victorian national emblem, Epacris impressa [Section 174] with wiry branches clad with pink tubular flowers.

plants.name: Hibbertia vestita
plants.context: At its base Hibbertia vestita [Section 174] is a small dense shrub brightened with open yellow flowers.

plants.name: Platytheca galioides
plants.context: Continue over the bridge, where in front of the tall Sydney Blue Gum, Eucalyptus saligna with pink-grey trunk, Platytheca galioides [Section 240] is a small plant with small purple flowers edging the branches.

plants.name: Correa 'Canberra Bells'
plants.context: A grouping of Correa ‘Canberra Bells’ [Section 240] small shrubs pretty with red and cream tubular flowers daintily hanging from its branches.

plants.name: Lechenaultia biloba
plants.context: Beside is a grouping of Lechenaultia biloba [Section 240] small plants displaying powder blue flowers.

plants.name: Epacris 'Nectar Pink'
plants.context: Opposite, in the Ellis Rowan garden Epacris ‘Nectar Pink’ [Section 131] is quite stunning with its long branches clad with pink and white tubular flowers.

plants.name: Crowea 'Cooper's Hybrid'
plants.context: Crowea ‘Cooper’s Hybrid’ [Section 240] is quite a large dense shrub displaying its pink star flowers.

plants.name: Eucalyptus 'Summer Red'
plants.context: Around the corner to the right is Eucalyptus ‘Summer Red’ [Section 240], a small upright tree displaying its large open fluffy red flowers and many buds, among the upper foliage.

plants.name: Callistemon viminalis
plants.context: Opposite is a grove of bottlebrushes, Callistemon viminalis [Section 310] tall shrubs with red bottlebrushes dangling from the arching branches

plants.name: Callistemon 'Baroondah Station'
plants.context: There also is Callistemon ‘Baroondah Station’ [Section 320] displaying its smaller soft pink bottlebrushes.

plants.name: Viola hederacea
plants.context: At the entrance to the Education Centre there is a dense groundcover of native violets, Viola hederacea [Section 320] profuse with small white and purple flowers.

plants.name: Banksia 'Giant Candles'
plants.context: Opposite the violets Banksia ‘Giant Candles’ [Section311] is a large shrub with quite long rust coloured juvenile flower spikes which will mature to a gold colour.

plants.name: Eustrephus latifolius
plants.context: The orange fruits seen among other shrubs are those of the vine, Wombat Berry, Eustrephus latifolius[Section 127].

plants.name: Pandorea jasminoides
plants.context: A vine, Pandorea jasminoides [Section 124] with large white flowers, climbs over shrubs

plants.name: Scaevola albida
plants.context: While below, a dense groundcover, Scaevola albida [Section 124] has a covering of small pink fan-shaped flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Goldfever'
plants.context: Grevillea ‘Goldfever’ [Section 124] is a small dense shrub bearing apricot coloured flowers

plants.name: Grevillea 'White Wings'
plants.context: While around the corner Grevillea ‘White Wings’ [Section 124] is of medium size with fine foliage and sprinkled with feathery white flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Poorinda Royal Mantle'
plants.context: The corner is clad with Grevillea ‘Poorinda Royal Mantle’ [Section 124] a dense groundcover with deep red toothbrush-like flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea bipinnatifida 'Jingle Bells'
plants.context: In the centre is an upright shrub, Grevillea bipinnatifida ‘Jingle Bells’ [Section 124] crowned with prickly divided leaves so attractive with its terminal long red-orange flower clusters.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: The orchid displays, inside the Visitor Centre are colourful and forever changing. The flowers edging the Banks Walk are colourful. However this walk follows the road on the far side of the Rainforest.

plants.name: Acacia fauntleroyi
plants.context: A wattle, Acacia fauntleroyi [Section 128], behind the cafe, is a tall hairy trunk, has fine leaves and a scattering of yellow flower balls.

plants.name: Clerodendrum floribundum var. attenuatum
plants.context: Almost opposite, edging the Rainforest, Clerodendrum floribundum var. attenuatum [Section 125] is a tall upright shrub with thin spotted trunk, and among the foliage are the smooth scarlet calyx surrounding large green fruit.

plants.name: Crinum pedunculatum
plants.context: Edging the road Swamp Lillies, Crinum pedunculatum [Section 125] are large bulbous plants with long narrow fleshy leaves and sprays of open white flowers on long stems.

plants.name: Grevillea bipinnatifolia 'Jingle Bells'
plants.context: In a corner Grevillea bipinnatifolia ‘Jingle Bells’ [Section 124] stands tall with terminal red flower sprays brightening the surrounding foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Goldfever'
plants.context: Grevillea ‘Goldfever’ [Section 124] continues to bear apricot coloured spider-like flowers over a low spreading shrub.

plants.name: Acronychia imperforata
plants.context: Acronychia imperforata [Sections 114,104] is a tall dense shrub with large shiny leaves and clusters of creamish rounded fruits in clusters

plants.name: Gahnia clarkei
plants.context: A Tall Saw-sedge, Gahnia clarkei [Section 78] is dense with long narrow rough edged leaves and long stems with black plumes.

plants.name: Epacris calvertiana
plants.context: The triangle garden contains Epacris calvertiana [Section 17] a dense wiry plant with small white tubular flowers edging the stems, while

plants.name: Chamelaucium 'Cascade Brook'
plants.context: Beside, a Geraldton Wax, Chamelaucium ‘Cascade Brook’ [Section 17] is a many branched shrub crowned with many pink wax open flowers.

plants.name: Leptospermum amboinense
plants.context: Leptospermum amboinense [Section 104,140] is a dense many branched shrub profuse with white petalled flowers.

plants.name: Hibiscus splendens
plants.context: Hibiscus splendens [Section 104] displays its few deep pink flowers and many buds among the dull rough foliage.

plants.name: Eucalyptus pulverulenta
plants.context: Turning right at the stairs beside which is the Silver-leaved Mountain Gum, Eucalyptus pulverulenta [Section 36] a small upright tree with silvery grey, almost rounded leaves appearing to be attached to the trunk.

plants.name: Banksia speciosa
plants.context: Almost surrounding is Banksia speciosa [Section 36], a large dense shrub with long narrow deeply indented leaves and still with grey-green acorn shaped flower spikes.

plants.name: Banksia media
plants.context: Follow the path to the right passing numerous banksias, mostly with small juvenile flower spikes also Banksia media [Section 36], a low misshapen dense shrub displaying mature cinnamon coloured compact flower spikes.

plants.name: Telopea mongaensis
plants.context: Close to the covered shelter a waratah, Telopea mongaensis [Section 36] with out-of-season inferior red flower heads.

plants.name: Banksia marginata
plants.context: Beside is Banksia marginata [Section 36] a tall dense shrub local to the area, well clad with short yellow flower spikes.

plants.name: Grevillea beadleana
plants.context: There too, is Grevillea beadleana [Section 36], a low spreading shrub with soft green foliage and scattered with maroon coloured toothbrush like flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Few of the many flowers will be mentioned from the Information Centre to the end of the buildings. The walk then will venture up to the Rock Garden and then almost encircle the Eucalyptus Lawn.

plants.name: Allocasuarina littoralis
plants.context: At the base of the stairs to the Information Centre, a Sheoak, Allocasuarina littoralis [Section 174] spreads its branches clad with pine-like leaves and deep red rounded flowers, above the path.

plants.name: Prostanthera phylicifolia
plants.context: Prostanthera phylicifolia [Section 210] is a dense shrub falling over the rock wall, now clad with mauve flowers.

plants.name: Hibbertia vestita
plants.context: Below is Hibbertia vestita [Section 210] a low spreading shrub bright with open yellow flowers.

plants.name: Banksia 'Stumpy Gold'
plants.context: Following the Main Path, in the Ellis Rowan Garden, Banksia ‘Stumpy Gold’ [Section 131] is a dwarf spreading shrub with juvenile pencil thin upright dusky gold flower spikes (many banksias are now bearing juvenile flower spikes), some now are mature.

plants.name: Epacris longiflora
plants.context: Epacris longiflora [Section 131] has long wiry branches clad with bright red tube shaped flowers with white mouth while nearby

plants.name: Epacris 'Nectar Pink'
plants.context: Epacris ‘Nectar Pink’ [Sectiion 131] has soft pink tubular flowers.

plants.name: Callistemon citrinus 'Splendens'
plants.context: Almost concealed by a bottlebrush, Callistemon citrinus ‘Splendens’ [Section 240] a large shrub with bright red bottlebrush flowers is Eucalyptus ‘Summer Beauty’ [Section 240] which displays its soft pink feathery flowers.

plants.name: Eucalyptus 'Summer Beauty'
plants.context: Almost concealed by a bottlebrush, Callistemon citrinus ‘Splendens’ [Section 240] a large shrub with bright red bottlebrush flowers is Eucalyptus ‘Summer Beauty’ [Section 240] which displays its soft pink feathery flowers.

plants.name: Eucalyptus 'Summer Red'
plants.context: Around the corner Eucalyptus ‘Summer Red’ [Section 240] is dazzling with feathery red flowers and many buds, also on small trees.

plants.name: Thryptomene 'Pink Lace'
plants.context: At the corner of the building take the left road passing the Pryor Tree, Eucalyptus mannifera, below its branches, Thryptomene ‘Pink Lace’ [Section 10] in a group is a low spreading shrub pink with tiny flowers edging its branches.

plants.name: Correa alba var. alba
plants.context: Towards the Rock Garden, Correa alba var. alba [Section 107] has white star-shaped flowers scattered among the dull green leaves of the dense hedge-like shrub.

plants.name: Guichenotia ledifolia
plants.context: Opposite the scenic waterfall and ponds, Guichenotia ledifolia [Section 4] is a neat rounded shrub clad in profusion with down- turned cup-like mauve flowers.

plants.name: Acacia parvipinnula
plants.context: Follow the Main Path to a section of wattles where the perfumed Acacia parvipinnula [Section18] a tree clad with dark divided leaves and cream fluffy flower balls.

plants.name: Eucalyptus polybractea
plants.context: At the exit is a small tree, a Blue-leaved Mallee, Eucalyptus polybractea [Section 18] has conspicuous cream feathery flowers.

plants.name: Acacia uncinata
plants.context: On the far side close to the lawn, in a garden Acacia uncinata [Section 44] has bright yellow flower balls while close by Crowea saligna [Section 44] is a low open shrub with large pink star-like flowers.

plants.name: Crowea saligna
plants.context: On the far side close to the lawn, in a garden Acacia uncinata [Section 44] has bright yellow flower balls while close by Crowea saligna [Section 44] is a low open shrub with large pink star-like flowers.

plants.name: Actinotus helianthii
plants.context: The road then follows the Sydney Basin to the left where flannel flowers, Actinotus helianthii [Section 191l] are small plants with soft grey flannel-like foliage and the renowned large white many petalled flowers.

plants.name: Banksia aemula
plants.context: Down this road banksias include Banksia aemula [Section 191l, 191e], all large dense plants with lime coloured flower spikes.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa var. cunninghamii
plants.context: Banksia spinulosa var. cunninghamii, the Hairpin Banksia [Section 191e] has lemon, maturing to almost red flower spikes while

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia
plants.context: Banksia ericifolia [Section 191e], at a side path leading to the shade houses, has mature, almost red flower spikes.

plants.name: Correa 'Bett'
plants.context: At the next road junction, past the Eucalyptus Lawns, Correa ‘Bett’s Red’ [Section 112] is a dense small shrub bright with red tubular flowers while behind Correa ‘Canberra Bells' [Section 112] is less dense but displays its more robust red and lemon flower bells.

plants.name: Correa 'Canberra Bells
plants.context: At the next road junction, past the Eucalyptus Lawns, Correa ‘Bett’s Red’ [Section 112] is a dense small shrub bright with red tubular flowers while behind Correa ‘Canberra Bells' [Section 112] is less dense but displays its more robust red and lemon flower bells.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Such a pleasant autumn day to stroll along the Main Path which winds through magnificent eucalyptus trees, the Sydney Basin, the Rock Garden and the Rainforest. The walk starts at the far end of the cafe building close to Eucalyptus ‘Summer Red’ which shows off its fiery red flowers.

plants.name: Eucalyptus 'Summer Red'
plants.context: The walk starts at the far end of the cafe building close to Eucalyptus ‘Summer Red’ which shows off its fiery red flowers.

plants.name: Thryptomene sp
plants.context: Continue along the Main Path,passing Thryptomene sp.[Section 10], a low spreading shrub profuse with tiny pink flowers.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia
plants.context: This one is Banksia ericifolia [Section 30] which displays many juvenile and mature gold upright cylindrical flower spikes.

plants.name: Grevillea diminuta
plants.context: Behind the seat Grevillea diminuta [Section 30] is a rounded shrub with dangling clusters of rust coloured flowers among the dull green foliage.

plants.name: Banksia 'Birthday Candles'
plants.context: Banksia ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 30] has many juvenile and matured golden flower spikes on the dwarf spreading shrub while

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia
plants.context: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia [Section 30] is a prostrate plant with lemon spikes among the dull green, silver backed leaves.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Coconut Ice'
plants.context: At the cross-roads, Grevillea ‘Coconut Ice’ [Section 25] is a now spreading shrub with interesting leaves and terminal sprays of pink-red flowers........today there are many yellow tailed black cockatoos flying above, all singing their own song.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Lady O
plants.context: Across the road, Grevillea ‘Lady O’ [Section 26] is also a low shrub with fiery red spider like flowers dangling from the lateral branches.

plants.name: Banksia marginata 'Cape Patterson Dwarf'
plants.context: Beside is Banksia marginata ‘Cape Patterson Dwarf’ [Section 26] of similar size with small green-gold flower spikes.

plants.name: Grevillea sericea
plants.context: Pass by many grevilleas and close to the next road Grevillea sericea [Section 30] has white spider-like flowers on the medium upright plant.

plants.name: Crowea exalata
plants.context: Across the road, among the grand mottled grey tree trunks of the gum trees, Crowea exalata [Section 112] is sparkling with small pink star-like flowers over the rounded shrub.

plants.name: Correa 'Canberra Bells'
plants.context: At the end of this section, Correa ‘Canberra Bells’ [Section 112] is small and so pretty with red and deep cream tube shaped flowers.

plants.name: Goodenia paniculata
plants.context: The small herb, Goodenia paniculata [Section 191h] is bright with small yellow flowers edging the stems.

plants.name: Telopea sp
plants.context: There also are waratahs, Telopea sp.

plants.name: Epacris calvertiana var. calvertilana
plants.context: Epacris calvertiana var. calvertilana [Section 191j] has small white tubular flowers edging its long wiry stems.

plants.name: Scaevola albida
plants.context: At the turn-off to the Display Glasshouse, Scaevola albida [Section 191j] has a profusion of small pink fan-shaped flowers over the low spreading plant.

plants.name: Hibbertia pedunculata
plants.context: In the Display Garden, Hibbertia pedunculata [Section 191u] a dense groundcover bright with yellow open petalled flowers.

plants.name: Actinotus helianthi
plants.context: There too is the renowned flannel flower, Actinotus helianthi [Section 191u, 191l] with soft white petalled flowers and velvet-grey foliage.

plants.name: Crowea saligna
plants.context: Behind the seat Crowea saligna [Section 191u] is a low spreading shrub displaying its large pink, so attractive flowers.

plants.name: Acacia subulata
plants.context: Stroll through the Eucalyptus Lawn dotted with a variety of trees and down to the wattle section where Acacia subulata [Section 18] is clad with soft yellow perfumed flower balls.

plants.name: Guichenotia ledifolia
plants.context: The Rock Garden abounds with interesting plants which include Guichenotia ledifolia [Section 4] a rounded shrub clad with down- turned pink cup shaped flowers.

plants.name: Pandorea jasminoides

plants.name: Swainsona formosa

plants.name: Anigozanthos 'Bush Volcano'
plants.context: Most kangaroo paws are finishing flowering, but Anigozanthos ‘Bush Volcano’ [Section 174] continues to bear its rust-red flowers.

plants.name: Anigozanthos 'Big Red'

plants.name: Eucryphia wilkiei
