plants.name: Chrysocephalum apiculatum
plants.context: At the bottom of the stairs the garden corner is colourful with the yellow button-sized flowers of Chrysocephalum apiculatum, the deep pink star-shaped flowers of Crowea ‘Festival’ and the red terminal flowers of Grevillea ‘Lady O’ [all in Section 174].

plants.name: Crowea 'Festival'
plants.context: At the bottom of the stairs the garden corner is colourful with the yellow button-sized flowers of Chrysocephalum apiculatum, the deep pink star-shaped flowers of Crowea ‘Festival’ and the red terminal flowers of Grevillea ‘Lady O’ [all in Section 174].

plants.name: Grevillea 'Lady O'
plants.context: At the bottom of the stairs the garden corner is colourful with the yellow button-sized flowers of Chrysocephalum apiculatum, the deep pink star-shaped flowers of Crowea ‘Festival’ and the red terminal flowers of Grevillea ‘Lady O’ [all in Section 174].

plants.name: Ceratopetalum gummiferum
plants.context: Admire the NSW Christmas Bush, Ceratopetalum gummiferum [Section 142], below the carpark at the entrance to the Tasmanian section.

plants.name: Alocasia macrorrhizos
plants.context: This walk then returns to the road edging the Rainforest where, opposite the cafe, the Cunjevoi Lily, Alocasia macrorrhizos [Section 125], has large fleshy spade-like leaves and stems with green or yellow hood-like flowers.

plants.name: Crinum pedunculatum
plants.context: The Swamp Lily, Crinum pedunculatum [Sections 306 and 125], displays its open sprays of white flowers on long upright stems.

plants.name: Clerodendrum floribundum
plants.context: Clerodendrum floribundum [Section 125] is a tall shrub with button-sized green fruits in enlarged roughened red calyces seen among its foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea bipinnatifida 'Jingle Bells'
plants.context: Standing tall in this corner, Grevillea bipinnatifida ‘Jingle Bells’ [Section124] looks grand with its large red flower spikes flowing down among its greenery.

plants.name: Callistemon 'Howie's Fireglow'
plants.context: A backdrop is a bottlebrush, Callistemon ‘Howie’s Fireglow’ [Section 124], brilliant with its red flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Poorinda Royal Mantle'
plants.context: The corner groundcover is Grevillea ‘Poorinda Royal Mantle’ [Section 124] with many toothbrush-like dark red flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Goldfever'
plants.context: Grevillea ‘Goldfever’ [Section 124] has apricot-coloured flowers on the low lateral branches.

plants.name: Callistemon montanus
plants.context: Continuing uphill, Callistemon montanus [Section 104] is bright with short crimson bottlebrushes, seen as it leans towards the road.

plants.name: Leptospermum amboinense
plants.context: Close by a teatree, Leptospermum amboinense [Section 104] is a large dense shrub prolific with small daisy-like flowers.

plants.name: Chamelaucium 'Cascade Brook'
plants.context: In this triangular garden a Geraldton Wax, Chamelaucium ‘Cascade Brook’ [Section 17], has a profusion of waxy pale pink flowers on the dense shrub.

plants.name: Brachyscome multifida 'Breakoday'
plants.context: On the other side are Brachyscome multifida ‘Breakoday’ [Section 17], small dense plants with fine foliage and small deep mauve daisy-like flowers.

plants.name: Callistemon viminalis
plants.context: Opposite is Callistemon viminalis [Section 78], a quite large shrub with pleasant weeping habit and bright red bottlebrushes.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Such a pleasant autumn day to stroll along the Main Path which winds through the Sydney Basin, the Eucalypt Lawn, the Rock Garden and the Rainforest. The walk commences at the far end of the cafe building and will select only a few plants in flower.

plants.name: Callistemon viminalis
plants.context: Callistemon viminalis [Section 310] at the corner is a tall shrub with many branches and a covering of dark red bottlebrushes.

plants.name: Callistemon chisholmii
plants.context: Callistemon chisholmii [Sections 10, 11] arching above the path has a weeping habit and smaller pink flowers.

plants.name: Babingtonia 'Howie's Feathertips'
plants.context: Beside the seat, Babingtonia ‘Howie’s Feathertips’ [Section 30] is an upright shrub bright with tiny white-petalled flowers.

plants.name: Banksia 'Birthday Candles'
plants.context: Banksia ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 30] (like many other banksias) is now bearing green pencil-thin flower spikes with a few changing colour to a gold tone.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Lady O'
plants.context: At the next corner, the popular Grevillea ‘Lady O’ [Sections 26, 24] is a low shrub with lateral branches bearing its clusters of lovely red flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Pink Lady'
plants.context: Behind this, Grevillea ‘Pink Lady’ [Section 24] conceals its interesting pink-cream flowers in the low dense shrub.

plants.name: Banksia marginata 'Cape Patterson Dwarf'
plants.context: Banksia marginata ‘Cape Patterson Dwarf’ [Section 26] has immature lime flower spikes among the dark foliage.

plants.name: Persoonia acerosa
plants.context: A Geebung, Persoonia acerosa [Section 26], has bright green foliage dotted with tiny yellow tube-shaped flowers on this dense, almost rounded shrub.

plants.name: Banksia conferta
plants.context: Pass by an aging Banksia conferta subsp.

plants.name: Crowea exalata
plants.context: Across the road, at the next corner, Crowea exalata [Section 112] has tiny pink star flowers.

plants.name: Correa 'Canberra Bells'
plants.context: At the next exit, a group of Correa ‘Canberra Bells’ [Section 112].This small open shrub commemorates Canberra’s centenary (1913–2013) and bears attractive bright red- cream bell-shaped flowers.

plants.name: Actinotus helianthi
plants.context: One of the highlights is the flannel flower, Actinotus helianthi [Sections 191h, 191s].

plants.name: Scaevola ramosissima
plants.context: Edging the side road is Scaevola ramosissima [Section 191h], a prostrate plant with deep purple flowers on its trailing stems.

plants.name: Goodenia paniculata
plants.context: Here too is a Goodenia paniculata [Section 191h], also prostrate but with yellow flowers.

plants.name: Scaevola albida
plants.context: At the turn-off to the glasshouse, Scaevola albida [Section 191j] is a dense prostrate plant bearing tiny pink fan-shaped flowers.

plants.name: Acacia linifolia
plants.context: A wattle, Acacia linifolia [Section 191e], with clusters of lemon fluffy flower balls can be seen among other shrubs.

plants.name: Crowea saligna
plants.context: Behind the round seat, Crowea saligna [Section 191u] is an attractive plant with prominent bright pink star-like flowers among the light green foliage.

plants.name: Acacia fulva
plants.context: These include Acacia fulva [Section 18], well clad with lemon fluffy flower balls.

plants.name: Platytheca galioides
plants.context: At the entrance are pots which include Platytheca galioides [Section 15r], a loose branched plant with small blue flowers.

plants.name: Syzygium australe
plants.context: In the coolness of the Rainforest Syzygium australe [Section 148] is a shrub rising above the board-walk, showing its white fluffy flowers among its dark green leaves.

plants.name: Eucryphia wilkiei
plants.context: At the exit of the Rainforest a Leatherwood, Eucryphia wilkiei [Section 313], is a dense shrub profuse with its cream cup-shaped flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: The shrub pictured above, selected to commemorate Canberra’s centenary in 2013, will be seen on this walk as well as many other flowers. The walk starts at the doors of the Visitor Information Centre.

plants.name: Rhododendron viriosum
plants.context: Rhododendron viriosum, growing in a pot but originally from far north Queensland, displays its attractive orange-red bell-shaped flowers.

plants.name: Swainsona formosa
plants.context: Swainsona formosa, from the arid areas of our country, is also attractive with large pea-shaped bright red flowers with dark centres.

plants.name: Hibbertia vestita
plants.context: Edging Banks Walk Hibbertia vestita [Section 174] has bright yellow open flowers over the dense ground cover.

plants.name: Corymbia 'Summer Red'
plants.context: In the centre of this bed is a small tree, Corymbia ‘Summer Red’ [Section 174], showy with clusters of red flowers.

plants.name: Anigozanthos 'Bush Pioneer'
plants.context: Kangaroo Paws are finishing, however Anigozanthos ‘Bush Pioneer’ [Section 174] still reveals its yellow-green paw flowers on long upright stems.

plants.name: Crinum pedunculatum
plants.context: Take the road on the far side of the Rainforest Gully where outside the cafe the Swamp Lily, Crinum pedunculatum [Sections 306 and 125], displays its open sprays of white flowers.

plants.name: Alocasia macrorrhizos
plants.context: Opposite, the Cunjevoi Lily, Alocasia macrorrhizos [Section 125], with large spade-like fleshy leaves has green or yellow hood-like flowers on long stems.

plants.name: Clerodendrum floribundum
plants.context: Another interesting plant is Clerodendrum floribundum [Section 125], a small tree with button-sized green fruits in enlarged red calyces seen among its rather dense foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea bipinnatifida 'Jingle Bells'
plants.context: Continuing along this road, Grevillea bipinnatifida ‘Jingle Bells’ [Section 124] is grown as a standard.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Poorinda Royal Mantle'
plants.context: Surrounding it is Grevillea ‘Poorinda Royal Mantle’ [Section 124], a dense groundcover bearing dark red toothbrush-like flowers.

plants.name: Scaevola 'Mauve Clusters'
plants.context: Around the corner, Scaevola ‘Mauve Clusters’ [Section 124] is also a groundcover with small fan-shaped mauve flowers falling over the rock wall.

plants.name: Scaevola albida
plants.context: Scaevola albida [Section 124] is similar but its fan-shaped flowers are a pale blue.

plants.name: Eucalyptus mannifera
plants.context: Across the road our grand old Eucalyptus mannifera [Section 10] has lost another of its large mottled white branches.

plants.name: Eremophila strongylophylla
plants.context: Continuing on the road to the left, an emu bush, Eremophila strongylophylla [Section 302], is a low spreading plant with green-grey foliage and prominent purple bugle- shaped flowers.

plants.name: Correa 'Canberra Bells'
plants.context: At this corner is a group of small open shrubs of Correa ‘Canberra Bells’ [Section 119].

plants.name: Correa alba var. alba
plants.context: Correa alba var. alba [Section 107] is a dense spreading shrub of medium height, with grey-green silver-edged leaves and cream four-petalled flowers.

plants.name: Epacris longiflora
plants.context: Towards the Rock Garden, Epacris longiflora [Section 110] is rather a straggly shrub with tubular flowers coloured red with white mouths hanging in rows from the upright branches.

plants.name: Callistemon pachyphyllus 'Smoked Salmon'
plants.context: A bottlebrush, Callistemon pachyphyllus ‘Smoked Salmon’ [Section 110], bears few pale salmon-coloured flowers on the medium size shrub.

plants.name: Swainsona galegifolia
plants.context: Close by is Swainsona galegifolia [Section 110] with upright branches bearing mauve-pink pea-shaped flowers

plants.name: Geissois biagiana
plants.context: On the top of the waterfall is a small tree, Geissois biagiana [Section 15q], so prominent with its crown of bright red new leaves.

plants.name: Eremophila bignoniiflora × polyclada
plants.context: At the exit to this area, between the flower pots, is another emu bush, Eremophila bignoniiflora × polyclada [Section 15r].

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: This walk follows a path with maybe not so many flowers but it is quite pleasant.

plants.name: Rhododendron viriosum
plants.context: Plants in pots outside the Visitor Information Centre include Rhododendron viriosum, attractive with its orange-red bell-shaped flowers, and the Sturt’s Desert Pea, Swainsona formosa, with its bright red dark-centred pea-shaped flowers.

plants.name: Swainsona formosa
plants.context: Plants in pots outside the Visitor Information Centre include Rhododendron viriosum, attractive with its orange-red bell-shaped flowers, and the Sturt’s Desert Pea, Swainsona formosa, with its bright red dark-centred pea-shaped flowers.

plants.name: Corymbia 'Summer Red'
plants.context: Along Banks Walk a small tree, Corymbia ‘Summer Red’ [Section 174] bears clusters of bright red flowers.

plants.name: Crowea 'Festival'

plants.name: Grevillea bipinnatifida 'Jingle Bells'

plants.name: Grevillea 'Goldfever'

plants.name: Callistemon citrinus 'Firebrand'

plants.name: Lambertia inermis

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia subsp

plants.name: Banksia conferta

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa
plants.context: Opposite, Banksia spinulosa [Section 27] is a small dense shrub with prominent dull gold upright immature flower spikes.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Lady O'
plants.context: At the next corner is Grevillea ‘Lady O’ [Sections 26, 24], with bright red flower clusters on this low spreading shrub.

plants.name: Banksia robur

plants.name: Grevillea rhyolitica subsp. rhyolitica
plants.context: Deua Flame, Grevillea rhyolitica subsp. rhyolitica [Section 25], is also a large shrub bearing red spider-like flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea diminuta
plants.context: Grevillea diminuta [Section 25] is another large shrub with strands of rust-coloured flowers dangling from the branches.

plants.name: Banksia aemula
plants.context: Almost opposite, Banksia aemula [Section 24] is a large dense shrub with many lemon flower spikes.

plants.name: Thomasia petalocalyx
plants.context: Edging the road, Thomasia petalocalyx [Section 25] is low and dense, sprinkled with small pink downturned flowers.

plants.name: Westringia glabra
plants.context: Past the zebra crossing, Westringia glabra [Section 6] is a medium open shrub bearing small mauve flowers.

plants.name: Correa alba
plants.context: Correa alba [Sections 7, 107] has a covering of white star flowers over the dense shrub.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Robyn Gordon'

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: This walk is around and about the Rock Garden where flowers are forever changing but firstly enjoy those along Banks Walk. Then follow the road on the far side of the Rain Forest turning right at the intersection with the Main Path which will reach the waterfall in the Rock Garden.

plants.name: Hibbertia serpyllifolia
plants.context: At the corner Hibbertia serpyllifolia [Section 15c] is a low spreading shrub with small open yellow flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea lanigera
plants.context: Grevillea lanigera [Section 15c] is semi-prostrate and dense with pale pink flowers.

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia
plants.context: Ascending the stairs Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia [Section 15c] is a dense low-growing plant with dull green foliage and green-yellow flower spikes plus many thin green immature flower spikes.

plants.name: Correa 'Ivory Bells'
plants.context: Opposite, Correa ‘Ivory Bells’ [Section 15d] has a profusion of tubular cream flowers over this medium-sized dense shrub.

plants.name: Banksia 'Honeypots'
plants.context: Close beside is Banksia ‘Honeypots’ [Section 15d], a small upright plant with its cylindrical upright honey-coloured flower spikes.

plants.name: Chrysocephalum semipapposum
plants.context: Chrysocephalum semipapposum [Section 15d] adds brightness to the area with dazzling button-size orange flowers over the spreading plant.

plants.name: Persicaria decipiens
plants.context: Crowded beside the bridge the Slender Knotweed, Persicaria decipiens [Section 15d], is a vigorous semi-aquatic plant with terminal stems clad with tiny pink flowers.

plants.name: Hypocalymma xanthopetalum
plants.context: Hypocalymma xanthopetalum [Section 15f] has tiny yellow frilly flowers along its branches.

plants.name: Allocasuarina rigida
plants.context: Around this section is a group of mountain she-oaks, Allocasuarina rigida [Section 15a], clad with ochre-coloured needle-thin male flowers suspended from the branches.

plants.name: Plectranthus graveolens
plants.context: At the base of these stairs, Plectranthus graveolens [Section 15a] is a herbaceous plant with large felt-like leaves and prominent spikes of pale blue flowers.

plants.name: Prostanthera staurophylla
plants.context: There too is Prostanthera staurophylla [Section 15a], a low compact spreading shrub with mauve flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Mason's Hybrid'
plants.context: The large spreading shrub opposite is Grevillea ‘Mason’s Hybrid’ [Section 15h], crowned with its large terminal cream flower clusters with long curved red stamens.

plants.name: Anigozanthos flavidus
plants.context: From the top road an attractive kangaroo paw, Anigozanthos flavidus [Section 15h], is visible with its copper-coloured “paw” flowers tipping the long slender stems.

plants.name: Scaevola albida var. albida
plants.context: Edging the path, Scaevola albida var. albida [Section 15h] is a semi-prostrate dense plant clad with mauve fan-shaped flowers.

plants.name: Xerochrysum bracteatum
plants.context: Across the road the self-seeding yellow straw daisy flowers are those of Xerochrysum bracteatum [Section 3].

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Birthday Candles'
plants.context: Take the downward path between the grass trees, Xanthorrhoea johnsonii [Sections 15,14] to Banksia spinulosa ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 15 l], a dwarf spreading shrub with mainly dull green flower spikes yet to mature to their full golden colour.

plants.name: Acacia aneura var. aneura
plants.context: Close by is a wattle, Acacia aneura var. aneura [Section 15 l] a shrub of medium size with interesting short yellow rod-like inflorescences among the grey-green foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea sp
plants.context: From the other side of the downward path, beside a seat is a Grevillea sp. [Section 15k], an ageing plant with trunk hugging the ground and upright branches clad with toothbrush- like deep red flowers and many buds.

plants.name: Verticordia pennigera
plants.context: Follow the downward path where, in a pot, Verticordia pennigera [Section 15r] has small bright pink feathery flowers over the low spreading plant.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: A stroll along the Main Path this time of the year is a pleasant experience. Starting at the end of the café building, this walk meanders through the Sydney Region Basin, the Rock Garden and the Rainforest.

plants.name: Thryptomene sp
plants.context: Thryptomene sp. [Section 10] is a fairly open shrub of medium height with branches clad with tiny pink-petalled flowers.

plants.name: Banksia heliantha
plants.context: Continue on past the bed of daisies to view Banksia heliantha [Section 30].

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Honeypots'
plants.context: Close by is Banksia spinulosa ‘Honeypots’ [Section 30], bearing honey-coloured upright cylindrical flower spikes.

plants.name: Callistemon 'Reeves Pink'
plants.context: Almost opposite, Callistemon ‘Reeves Pink’ [Section 30] bears its lovely pink bottlebrush flowers.

plants.name: Reeves Pink'
plants.context: Almost opposite, Callistemon ‘Reeves Pink’ [Section 30] bears its lovely pink bottlebrush flowers.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia 'Red Clusters'
plants.context: Banksia ericifolia ‘Red Clusters’ [Section 25] is a tall slim shrub bright with its colourful flower spikes.

plants.name: Grevillea sericea subsp. sericea
plants.context: Grevillea sericea subsp. sericea [Section 27] is a medium open shrub bearing cream lacy flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'LadyO'
plants.context: Crossing the road, Grevillea ‘LadyO’ [Section 26] is a low shrub with red flowers pendent from its lateral branches.

plants.name: Banksia conferta subsp. penicillata
plants.context: Banksia conferta subsp. penicillata [Section 26] is a large ageing shrub laden mostly with old dark flower spikes also with mature lemon flower spikes.

plants.name: Grevillea juniperina 'Molonglo'
plants.context: Grevillea juniperina ‘Molonglo’ [Section 24] is a prostrate shrub with apricot-coloured flowers on the long lateral branches.

plants.name: Acradenia frankliniae
plants.context: Across the next road, almost concealed by other shrubs, Acradenia frankliniae [Section 112] is a medium-sized shrub with glossy green leaves and a profusion of small balloon-shaped buds opening to cream star‑shaped flowers.

plants.name: Correa 'Canberra Bells'
plants.context: Before crossing the road to the Sydney Region Gully admire Correa ‘Canberra Bells’ [Section 112], graceful with its pendulous red tubular flowers with yellow mouths.

plants.name: Actinotus helianthi
plants.context: At the entrance in a newly-developed area there are many flannel flowers, Actinotus helianthi [Sections 191h, 191s].

plants.name: Crowea exalata
plants.context: Edging the path Crowea exalata [Section 191h] has small pink star-shaped flowers over the low dense shrub.

plants.name: Scaevola albida
plants.context: At the corner, where a path leads to the Display Glasshouse, Scaevola albida [Section 191j] is a dense groundcover profuse with small fan-shaped mauve flowers.

plants.name: Crowea saligna
plants.context: In the display garden, behind the circular seat, Crowea saligna [Section 191u] is a low spreading long-flowering shrub profuse with bright pink star-shaped flowers among the waxy bright green foliage.

plants.name: Prostanthera porcata
plants.context: Here also is Prostanthera porcata [Section 191u], a taller open shrub with pink tubular flowers.

plants.name: Scaevola ramosissima
plants.context: At the exit, near more flannel flowers, is Scaevola ramosissima [Section 191 l].

plants.name: Xerochrysum sp
plants.context: Follow the curved path through the Eucalyptus Lawn down to the Rock Garden, which is brightened with a grouping of large yellow straw flowers, Xerochrysum sp.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Birthday Candles'
plants.context: In front of the attractive waterfall and pools is Banksia spinulosa ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 15v], bright with its golden flower spikes.

plants.name: Rhododendron lochiae × macgregoriae

plants.name: Prostanthera phylicifolia
plants.context: Nearby is a mint bush, Prostanthera phylicifolia [Section 210], a dense shrub clad in profusion with small mauve flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: This walk is to view flowers in the Mallee Section, which contains species from South and Western Australia. It will also pass by the Red Centre Garden construction site, starting from the Ducrou Pavilion.

plants.name: Lechenaultia formosa

plants.name: Nicotiana rosulata subsp. ingulba

plants.name: Swainsona formosa
plants.context: Close by is an area with Sturt’s Desert Pea, Swainsona formosa, scattered among the rocks.

plants.name: Chrysocephalum apiculatum
plants.context: Opposite is Chrysocephalum apiculatum [Section 300] with its small orange flower heads draped over the wall.

plants.name: Maireana sedifolia
plants.context: A blue-bush, Maireana sedifolia [Section 100b], covers its small branches with grey fleshy leaves.

plants.name: Eremophila warnesii

plants.name: Eremophila alternifolia

plants.name: Lechenaultia biloba
plants.context: Lechenaultia biloba [Section 100b] bears its powder blue flowers on long meandering stems.

plants.name: Thryptomene denticulata
plants.context: Thryptomene denticulata [Section 100b] is a small open shrub with fine foliage and tiny pink flowers edging the stems

plants.name: Dampiera salahae
plants.context: Close by the tiny Dampiera salahae [Section 100b] is clad with blue flowers.

plants.name: Thomasia petalocalyx
plants.context: Rounding the corner, Thomasia petalocalyx [Section 100a] is a dense medium shrub with many small pink downturned flowers.

plants.name: Banksia epica

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: This walk, although somewhat longer, provides many plants to admire including a variety of interesting shrubs. It starts just past the café building.

plants.name: Swainsona formosa

plants.name: Callistemon citrinus 'Splendens'

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Light fogs and frosts followed by lovely sunny days are ideal to view our autumn display, especially banksias which are now bursting into flower.

plants.name: Lechenaultia formosa

plants.name: Banksia heliantha

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: A walk along the curvaceous Main Path this time of the year is a pleasant experience. Flowers are plentiful which includes many banksias. The walk commences at the far end of the café building.

plants.name: Callistemon citrinus

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens

plants.context: Alyogyne huegelii [Section 100b] bears large white hibiscus-like flowers.

plants.name: Dampiera dysantha
plants.context: Opposite in a group is Dampiera dysantha [Section 100a], a small suckering plant displaying its intensely blue flowers.

plants.name: Pimelea lehmanniana
plants.context: Here too is Pimelea lehmanniana [Section 100a], with many upright stems having large terminal cream flower heads.

plants.name: Boronia crenulata var. crenulata
plants.context: Around the curve is Boronia crenulata var. crenulata [Sections 100b, 100c], as yet small plants clad with tiny pink flowers.

plants.name: Verticordia chrysantha
plants.context: Behind are Feather Flowers, Verticordia chrysantha [Section 100a], small plants bright with a canopy of yellow flowers.

plants.name: Chorizema cordatum
plants.context: Rounding the corner, Chorizema cordatum [Section 100a] is a rounded heap of branches clad with small red-orange pea- shaped flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea tripartita subsp
plants.context: Grevillea tripartita subsp.

plants.name: Pelargonium rodneyanum
plants.context: Pelargonium rodneyanum [Section 100c] is a low spreading plant with soft geranium-like leaves and magenta flowers.

plants.name: Hibbertia cuneiformis
plants.context: Hibbertia cuneiformis [Section 100c] has bright yellow flowers over the dense shrub.

plants.name: Micromyrtus ciliata
plants.context: Micromyrtus ciliata [Section 100a] is another attractive low mounded plant, clad well with dull red flowers.

plants.name: Senna artemisioides
plants.context: Senna artemisioides [Section 100a] is a low-growing plant bright with open yellow flowers.

plants.name: Xanthosia rotundifolia
plants.context: Southern Cross, Xanthosia rotundifolia [Section 100c] is a low rambling plant seen among other plants, with unique flower heads which form a white cross.

plants.name: Pimelea ferruginea 'Magenta Mist'
plants.context: Returning to the road, on the opposite side view the group of Pimelea ferruginea ‘Magenta Mist’ [Section 41], with heads of deep pink flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: This walk follows the Main Path, commencing at the far end of the Café building. It wanders among magnificent trees, through the Sydney Basin close to the new Red Centre Garden, then to the Rock Garden and the Rainforest Gully.

plants.name: Melaleuca fulgens 'Hot Pink'
plants.context: Melaleuca fulgens ‘Hot Pink’ [Section 10] has clusters of cheery pink flower clusters on the rather leggy shrub.

plants.name: Eremaea beaufortioides var. microphylla
plants.context: In a pot is Eremaea beaufortioides var. microphylla [Section 10], a small shrub clad with small orange flower balls.

plants.name: Melaleuca diosmifolia
plants.context: Melaleuca diosmifolia [Section 9] has many lime-coloured bottlebrush-like flowers among the small leaves of the dense shrub.

plants.name: Xanthorrhoea glauca
plants.context: The Grass Tree, Xanthorrhoea glauca [Section 8], has tall spikes clad with tiny flowers and surrounded by a skirt of long flowing leaves.

plants.name: Bulbine glauca
plants.context: This garden is scattered with self-seeded Bulbine glauca, with yellow star-shaped flowers on long succulent stems.

plants.name: Telopea 'Canberry Gem'
plants.context: A Waratah, Telopea ‘Canberry Gem’ [Section 30], is a large dense shrub clad with many heads of red flowers.

plants.name: Alyogyne huegelii
plants.context: Close by is Alyogyne huegelii [Section 30], a large shrub laden with white hibiscus flowers.

plants.name: Homoranthus flavescens
plants.context: Across the path, Homoranthus flavescens [Section 30] is an interesting shrub with layered branches clad with yellow nectar-laden perfumed flowers.

plants.name: Banksia blechnifolia
plants.context: Banksia blechnifolia [Section 25] is a prostrate plant with upright indented leaves and small deep red immature flower heads.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Coconut Ice'
plants.context: At the intersection, Grevillea ‘Coconut Ice’ [Section 25] is a low spreading shrub bearing many large terminal reddish flower spikes.

plants.name: Isopogon anemonifolius
plants.context: Across the road Isopogon anemonifolius [Section 26] has yellow drumstick-like flower heads among its divided leaves.

plants.name: Persoonia chamaepitys
plants.context: A groundcover, Persoonia chamaepitys [Section 24], has short green pine-like leaves and yellow flowers of similar size.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Bonfire'
plants.context: Grevillea ‘Bonfire’ [Section 24] is a tall hedge-like shrub with fresh green foliage and with many terminal waxy curvaceous flowers.

plants.name: Eriostemon australasius
plants.context: Crossing the next road Eriostemon australasius [Section 112] is clad with five-petalled soft pink flowers.

plants.name: Boronia muelleri
plants.context: Beside it and of similar size is Boronia muelleri [Section 112], clad with tiny pink buds opening to four-petalled flowers.

plants.name: Actinotus helianthi
plants.context: Across the road in the Sydney Region Gully are Flannel Flowers, Actinotus helianthi [Section 191h, 191s], with their soft daisy-like white flowers and silvery-grey foliage.

plants.name: Tetratheca thymifolia
plants.context: At the turn-off to the Glasshouses is Blackeyed Susan, Tetratheca thymifolia [Section 191j], a low spreading shrub covered with down-turned pink flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea aspleniifolia
plants.context: After passing by many flowers, at the exit is Grevillea aspleniifolia [Section 191l].

plants.name: Helichrysum elatum 'Helping Hand'
plants.context: Stroll through the Eucalyptus Lawn to an area of wattles and Helichrysum elatum ‘Helping Hand’ [Section 18], a low spreading shrub with large white daisy flowers among the soft greyish leaves.

plants.name: Hakea archaeoides
plants.context: Across the road Hakea archaeoides [Section 20] is a tall shrub with many bottlebrush-like rust red/yellow dangling flower spikes.

plants.name: Kunzea pulchella
plants.context: Edging the path Kunzea pulchella [Section 15r] is a large shrub bright with red fluffy flower balls.

plants.name: Rhodanthe chlorocephala subsp. rosea
plants.context: The enclosure is pretty with pink and white daisies, Rhodanthe chlorocephala subsp. rosea [Section 4].

plants.name: Thelychiton speciosus
plants.context: Passing the waterfall and through the cool Rainforest, continue to the Visitor Information Centre where white Rock Orchids, Thelychiton speciosus, are still flowering.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Spring flowers in the Gardens are breathtaking, including those in the Rock Garden which is the focus of this walk. To arrive there, follow the road on the far side of the Rainforest Gully and turn right at its intersection with the Main Path to reach the Rock Garden waterfall.

plants.name: Hibbertia serpyllifolia
plants.context: In a clockwise direction at the base of the stairs, Hibbertia serpyllifolia [Section 15c] is a low, long-branched shrub with yellow-petalled flowers.

plants.name: Doryanthes excelsa
plants.context: Gymea Lily, Doryanthes excelsa [Section 15c] has a head of red flowers on a very long stem surrounded by long strappy leaves.

plants.name: Hibbertia pedunculata
plants.context: Hibbertia pedunculata [Section 15d] is a groundcover clinging to rocks.

plants.name: Grevillea manglesii subsp. ornithopoda
plants.context: Up the stairs, the large shrub clad with white lacy flowers is Grevillea manglesii subsp. ornithopoda [Section 15d].

plants.name: Pileanthus vernicosus
plants.context: Close by is Copper Cups, Pileanthus vernicosus [Section 15d], a small open shrub with coppery red flowers.

plants.name: Anigozanthos 'Regal Claw'
plants.context: Kangaroo Paws, Anigozanthos ‘Regal Claw’ [Section 15d], reveal their paw-like reddish-green flower heads on long bare stems.

plants.name: Leptospermum variabile
plants.context: The large many-branched shrub clad with small white-petalled flowers across the path is Leptospermum variabile [Section 15c].

plants.name: Banksia blechnifolia
plants.context: Not to be missed is Banksia blechnifolia [Section 15d], a prostrate plant dense with long upright deeply-lobed tough leaves.

plants.name: Verticordia galeata
plants.context: Verticordia galeata [Section 15f] are dwarf dense shrubs covered with yellow feathery flowers.

plants.name: Xanthorrhoea johnsonii
plants.context: Their immature green wavy flower spikes and older brown spikes of the Grass Trees, Xanthorrhoea johnsonii [Section15f], are displayed above the “grass skirt” of their leaves.

plants.name: Bulbine glauca
plants.context: At the base of the stairs, Bulbine glauca [Section 15a] is a succulent plant with terminal yellow star-like flowers on long stems surrounded by linear leaves.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Mason's Hybrid'
plants.context: Climbing the stairs, Grevillea ‘Mason’s Hybrid’ [Section 15h] is a spreading old shrub with long branches clad with terminal clusters of red-shaded flowers.

plants.name: Anigozanthos flavidus
plants.context: Edging the top road, Anigozanthos flavidus [Section 15h] has long stems with terminal red flowers.

plants.name: Scaevola albida
plants.context: Scaevola albida [Section 15h] has mauve fan-shaped flowers over the mounded plants.

plants.name: Thomasia petalocalyx
plants.context: Thomasia petalocalyx [Section 15h] has a profusion of small downturned pink flowers over the dense shrub.

plants.name: Homoranthus prolixus
plants.context: Around the next corner, Homoranthus prolixus [Section 15j] is attractive with branches clad with flattened terminal gold perfumed flower spikes falling over the rock wall.

plants.name: Verticordia pennigera
plants.context: Continue downward to where, in a pot, Verticordia pennigera [Section 15r] is a low shrub dense with pink feathery flowers.

plants.name: Senecio linearifolius var
plants.context: Behind is Senecio linearifolius var.

plants.name: Labichea lanceolata subsp. lanceolata
plants.context: Close by is Labichea lanceolata subsp. lanceolata [Section 15r], bearing yellow flowers with petals marked with a red dot.

plants.name: Alyogyne huegelii 'West Coast Gem'
plants.context: Alyogyne huegelii ’West Coast Gem’ [Section 15r] is of similar size and bright with purple hibiscus flowers.

plants.name: Kunzea pulchella
plants.context: At the bottom of this path turn to the left to view Kunzea pulchella [Section 15r], a dense large shrub beautified with stumpy red bottlebrush flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: We will walk along the Main Path today noting the wide variety of plants in flower. We start at the Visitor Information Centre.

plants.name: Pandorea jasminoides
plants.context: Look up to your left at the magnificent display of Pandorea jasminoides [Section 212] covering the wall in pink flowers.

plants.name: Jasminum simplicifolium subsp. suavissimum
plants.context: Now look behind to your right to see (and smell) Jasminum simplicifolium subsp. suavissimum [Section 221] or Forest Jasmine with its five starry white petals and its lovely scent.

plants.name: Anigozanthos hybrid 'Bush Volcano'
plants.context: Amongst an interesting collection of pots on your right is Anigozanthos hybrid ‘Bush Volcano’ [Section 174] with long lasting rusty-red paw flowers.

plants.name: Melaleuca linariifolia 'Seafoam'
plants.context: Cross over the bridge and look down across the lawn to your right to see Melaleuca linariifolia ‘Seafoam’ [Section 243] in full bloom with white, soft, fluffy flowers attracting a wide variety of insects.

plants.name: Leptospermum polygalifolium subsp. montanum
plants.context: Leptospermum polygalifolium subsp. montanum [Section 9] on your right is a small tree covered in white five petalled flowers with green centres.

plants.name: Anigozanthos flavidus
plants.context: To the left is a group of Anigozanthos flavidus [Section 8] in varying colours of green and red.

plants.name: Banksia blechnifolia
plants.context: Notice the reddish brown cones of the ground-hugging Banksia blechnifolia [Section 25] with new darker cones emerging under the fishbone foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea 'LadyO'
plants.context: On the right after crossing the road is the reliably long-flowering Grevillea ‘LadyO’ [Section 26] with red clusters of flowers on a neat bush.

plants.name: Grevillea sericea
plants.context: On your right is an airy bush of Grevillea sericea [Section 26] or Pink Spider Flower with its clusters of pink flowers.

plants.name: Kennedia macrophylla
plants.context: Look down to your right to see Kennedia macrophylla [Section 112] a vigorous green vine with trifoliate leaves and burnt orange pea flowers.

plants.name: Actinotus helianthi
plants.context: At the entrance to the Sydney Region Flora the iconic Flannel Flower, Actinotus helianthi, [Section 191s], is in full bloom with white star flowers with yellow grey centres and silver-grey divided foliage.

plants.name: Pomaderris cinerea
plants.context: On your right in a small tree from the south coast of NSW, Pomaderris cinerea [Section 191s] covered in dull yellow fluffy flowers.

plants.name: Blandfordia grandiflora
plants.context: On your left are Christmas Bells, Blandfordia grandiflora [Section 191h] with their characteristic yellow and red bells on slender stems.

plants.name: Patersonia sericea
plants.context: Below to your left is Patersonia sericea [ Section 191g] with three petalled violet flowers on short stems.

plants.name: Hibbertia pedunculata
plants.context: Hibbertia pedunculata [Section 191j] has masses of cheerful yellow flowers on a low bush.

plants.name: Melaleuca thymifolia
plants.context: Melaleuca thymifolia [Section 191g] is a small bush with fringed purple flowers.

plants.name: Olearia quercifolia
plants.context: A tall bush on your right is Olearia quercifolia [Section 191l] or Oak-leaf Daisy Bush with clusters of white flowers on long stalks.

plants.name: Grevillea aspleniifolia
plants.context: On your left is a large sprawling bush of Grevillea aspleniifolia [Section 191g] which has long linear foliage and red toothbrush flowers.

plants.name: Hibbertia scandens
plants.context: Hibbertia scandens [Section 15c] or Snake Vine is a popular and vigorous climber with large yellow flowers.

plants.name: Cuttsia viburnea
plants.context: Cuttsia viburnea [Section 146] is a small tropical tree with large elliptical leaves and heads of white fragrant flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: We will start our walk from the Visitor Information Centre (VIC) then head up the hill past the rear of the café.

plants.name: Blandfordia grandiflora
plants.context: As you leave the VIC there is a magnificent display of Christmas Bells, Blandfordia grandiflora [Section 221], in a pot.

plants.name: Swainsona formosa
plants.context: Now look on your right to see Swainsona formosa [Section 221] or Sturt’s Desert Pea, with its brilliant red flowers contrasting happily with the grey‑green divided foliage.

plants.name: Anigozanthos 'Bush Pioneer'
plants.context: Further on your right is Anigozanthos ‘Bush Pioneer’ [Section 174], a tall yellow-green Kangaroo Paw flower with red stems.

plants.name: Clerodendrum floribundum var. attenuatum
plants.context: Turn up the hill to see on your left Clerodendrum floribundum var. attenuatum [Section 125], or Lolly Bush, a small tree in full bloom with clusters of strongly-scented white flowers against dark green foliage.

plants.name: Cymbidium suave
plants.context: Cymbidium suave [Section 125] on your left is an orchid with sprays of small greenish flowers and strap-like foliage growing out of a log.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Poorinda Royal Mantle'
plants.context: To the right is a large area of the prostrate groundcover Grevillea ‘Poorinda Royal Mantle’ [Section 124], with masses of red toothbrush flowers and persistent attention from the birds.

plants.name: Melaleuca linariifolia 'Snowstorm'
plants.context: Melaleuca linariifolia ‘Snowstorm’ [Section 124] is a small tree with twisted branches, fine foliage and white fluffy flowers.

plants.name: Senna acclinis
plants.context: Senna acclinis [Section 104] is a small shrub with divided foliage and dark yellow pea blooms with long seed-pods forming.

plants.name: Hibiscus splendens
plants.context: On your left is a tall bush, Hibiscus splendens [Section 104], with broad shield-shaped leaves and large pink flowers with maroon centres.

plants.name: Anigozanthos flavidus
plants.context: On your right free-flowering Anigozanthos flavidus [Section 17] forms a mass of rusty red and green paw flowers.

plants.name: Leptospermum subglabratum
plants.context: Leptospermum subglabratum [Section 17] shows masses of five-petalled white star flowers with small green foliage.

plants.name: Chamelaucium uncinatum 'Murfit Rose'
plants.context: Turn right along the road to see Chamelaucium uncinatum ‘Murfit Rose’ [Section 17] with pink flowers fading to darker pink on an airy bush.

plants.name: Chrysocephalum apiculatum
plants.context: Chrysocephalum apiculatum [Section 17] has cheerful bright yellow flowers on attractive grey-green foliage.

plants.name: Veronica derwentiana subsp. derwentiana
plants.context: Veronica derwentiana subsp. derwentiana [Section 123] has terminal sprays of white flowers on lacy bright green foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea robusta
plants.context: Turn right down the mulched path to the Silky Oak, Grevillea robusta [Section 79], a large tree with divided foliage and long brushes of golden yellow flowers dripping with nectar.

plants.name: Austromyrtus tenuifolia
plants.context: A tall green bush on your right is Austromyrtus tenuifolia [Section 16] with masses of small white flowers.

plants.name: Podolobium aciculiferum
plants.context: Also on your left is an open bush with dark green sharp-pointed leaves, Podolobium aciculiferum [Section 15c], which has small bright yellow pea flowers.

plants.name: Babingtonia pluriflora
plants.context: Babingtonia pluriflora [Section 16] is a small tree with masses of tiny white flowers on small bright green foliage.

plants.name: Banksia aemula
plants.context: On the left is the Wallum Banksia or Banksia aemula [Section 15c], with lots of dark brown spent cones but also lots of small light green new cones.

plants.name: Babingtonia 'Howie's Feathertips'
plants.context: Babingtonia ‘Howie’s Feathertips’ [Section 110] is a large bush of dense light green foliage with masses of tiny white flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: We will walk from the Visitor Information Centre (VIC) along the Main Path today.

plants.name: Rhododendron viriosum
plants.context: At the door of the VIC is a pot containing Rhododendron viriosum [Section 224] with bright coral bell flowers and shiny green foliage.

plants.name: Banksia baxteri
plants.context: On the other side of the door is Banksia baxteri [Section 221] or Bird’s Nest Banksia, with tall spires of stiff, triangular pink-tipped foliage and green brush flowers.

plants.name: Spyridium burragorang
plants.context: Further on your right is Spyridium burragorang [Section 174] whose flower heads consist of a centre of tiny white flowers surrounded by large white bracts.

plants.name: Grevillea juncifolia
plants.context: On your left is a pot of Grevillea juncifolia [Section 210] with narrow bootlace leaves and long racemes of yellowish-white flowers.

plants.name: Syzygium sp
plants.context: Go over the bridge and past the café to see a Syzygium sp. [Section 131] on your left with plenty of fluffy white flowers and neat shiny foliage.

plants.name: Babingtonia pluriflora
plants.context: Go up the hill to see on the left Babingtonia pluriflora [Section 30], a tall shrub with drooping foliage.

plants.name: Stenocarpus angustifolius
plants.context: Stenocarpus angustifolius [Section 9] on your right has clusters of lemon flowers in attractive contrast to the lance-shaped light green foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Coconut Ice'
plants.context: On the right-hand side before you cross the road is Grevillea ‘Coconut Ice’ [Section 25], which has large pink spider flowers with long red styles.

plants.name: Crowea exalata
plants.context: Crowea exalata [Section 112] is a mounded bush of fine foliage with pink star flowers.

plants.name: Teucrium argutum
plants.context: Go into the Sydney Region Gully to see on your right Teucrium argutum [Section 191i], an upright groundcover with spires of purple flowers.

plants.name: Platysace lanceolata
plants.context: On your left is Platysace lanceolata [Section 191e], with white flower heads covering an open bush.

plants.name: Persoonia acerosa
plants.context: Also on your left is the Needle Geebung, Persoonia acerosa [Section 191e], with gold spikes of blooms on needle-like foliage.

plants.name: Podolobium aciculiferum
plants.context: Podolobium aciculiferum [Section 18] on your left has golden flowers and sharply-pointed dark green foliage.

plants.name: Eucalyptus macrocarpa
plants.context: Near the waterfall on your right is Eucalyptus macrocarpa or Mottlecah [Section 15s], with striking grey sword-like foliage and large red fluffy flowers.

plants.name: Lythrum salicaria
plants.context: Lythrum salicaria or Purple Loosestrife [Section 15v] has plumes of pink-purple flowers on light green foliage.

plants.name: Eremophila christopheri
plants.context: Eremophila christopheri [Section 15v] also on your right has mauve bell flowers on a small bush.

plants.name: Babingtonia 'Howie's Feathertips'
plants.context: Babingtonia ‘Howie’s Feathertips’ [Section 110] is a large bush of dense light green foliage with masses of tiny white flowers.

plants.name: Callistemon pachyphyllus 'Smoked Salmon'
plants.context: Turn left at the waterfall down the hill towards the VIC to see on the right Callistemon pachyphyllus ‘Smoked Salmon’ [Section 110] with pink brush flowers on stiff foliage.

plants.name: Callistemon brachyandrus
plants.context: Also on your right is Callistemon brachyandrus [Section 110], which has red flowers with gold tips.

plants.name: Eremophila maculata
plants.context: Eremophila maculata [Section 302] has bright pink tubular flowers on a small bush.

plants.name: Eremophila longifolia
plants.context: Eremophila longifolia [Section 302] is a small tree with long narrow leaves and pink tubular flowers.

plants.name: Eremophila strongylophylla
plants.context: On the left is Eremophila strongylophylla [Section 302] with bright purple bell flowers on grey-green foliage.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: We will start our walk from the Visitor Information Centre (VIC) then head up the hill past the rear of the café to the Rock Garden.

plants.name: Banksia serrata
plants.context: After you leave the VIC on the right there is a group of Banksia serrata [Section 174], also called Old Man Banksia or Saw Banksia, behind the sculpture of Sir Joseph Banks.

plants.name: Corymbia ficifolia 'Dwarf Orange'
plants.context: Now look up to your left to see Corymbia ficifolia ‘Dwarf Orange’ [Section 210], a small tree with brilliant orange fluffy blooms and dark green foliage.

plants.name: Persoonia pinifolia
plants.context: On the right is Persoonia pinifolia[Section 110] or Pine–leaved Geebung, a large weeping shrub with needle-like foliage and racemes of yellow pointed flowers.

plants.name: Hibbertia serpyllifolia
plants.context: First on your left is Hibbertia serpyllifolia [Section 15c] or Hairy Guinea Flower, showing very fine light green foliage with 5-petalled lemon flowers in profusion.

plants.name: Hibbertia pedunculata
plants.context: Hibbertia pedunculata [Section 15d] on your right has brighter yellow flowers and fine creeping foliage.

plants.name: Hibbertia vestita
plants.context: Lastly on your left is Hibbertia vestita [Section 15c], which is also known as the Hairy Guinea Flower (this is why common names can be confusing!).

plants.name: Grevillea albiflora
plants.context: Turn right and on your upper left is Grevillea albiflora [Section 15g] or White Spider Flower, a large sweet-smelling bush with long needle-like foliage and white brushes with prominent styles.

plants.name: Beaufortia decussata
plants.context: On your right is Beaufortia decussata [Section 15f], a small shrub with red fluffy flowers with green centres and neat, close foliage.

plants.name: Acacia aneura var. aneura
plants.context: Turn right and on your left Acacia aneura var. aneura [Section 15l], commonly known as Mulga, is in full bloom with gold fluffy balls on needle-like greyish-green foliage.

plants.name: Muehlenbeckia axillaris
plants.context: Turn left and on your left is Muehlenbeckia axillaris [Section 15l] forming a mat of tiny rounded leaves with masses of small yellow flowers.

plants.name: Eremophila alternifolia
plants.context: Turn right down the steps and on the left is Eremophila alternifolia [Section 15r] with pink tubular flowers on an open bush with upright foliage.

plants.name: Eremophila bignoniiflora × polyclada
plants.context: Eremophila bignoniiflora x polyclada [Section 15r] also on the left shows masses of large white tubular flowers with purple- spotted throats.

plants.name: Melaleuca nesophila
plants.context: On the far left is Melaleuca nesophila [Section 15r], an upright shrub with purplish-pink flowers fading to white, giving it a two-tone appearance.

plants.name: Lythrum salicaria
plants.context: Lythrum salicaria [Section 15s] or Purple Loosestrife has tall sprays of purple-pink flowers with red stems.

plants.name: Teucrium racemosum
plants.context: Teucrium racemosum [Section 15v] is a delicate small bush with narrow silvery leaves and white flowers with a prominent lip.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: We will start our walk today from the café and follow the Main Path, finishing near the Rock Garden.

plants.name: Syzygium sp
plants.context: After you leave the cafe on the left there is a Lilly Pilly or Syzygium sp. [Section 131], a tall shrub with very shiny leaves and powderpuff white flowers.

plants.name: Correa 'Canberra Bells'
plants.context: Further on your right is Correa ‘Canberra Bells’ [Section 240], a low spreading bush with red bell flowers with white tips.

plants.name: Callistemon viminalis
plants.context: As you turn up the hill to your left look up to the right to see the deep red flowers of Callistemon viminalis [Section 310], also called Weeping Bottlebrush.

plants.name: Melaleuca lanceolata subsp. lanceolata
plants.context: On your left is Melaleuca lanceolata subsp. lanceolata [Section 10] with white fluffy flowers on an airy bush with fine needle-like foliage.

plants.name: Callistemon sp
plants.context: A Callistemon sp. [Section 10], also on your left, is a small tree with pink brush-like flowers with gold tips.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Bronze Rambler'
plants.context: Look down on your right to see Grevillea ‘Bronze Rambler’ [Section 30], which is a popular low groundcover with divided foliage and red toothbrush flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Poorinda Adorning'
plants.context: Grevillea ‘Poorinda Adorning’[Section 27] on your right is a low, prickly groundcover with bright red flowers with long styles.

plants.name: Grevillea 'LadyO'
plants.context: On your right after crossing the road is Grevillea ‘LadyO’[Section 24], a long‑blooming shrub with red flowers and bright green foliage.

plants.name: Crowea exalata
plants.context: On your left Crowea exalata [Section 112] forms a mounded bush of fine foliage dotted with pink star flowers.

plants.name: Dampiera purpurea
plants.context: As you enter the Sydney Gully Region, on your left is Dampiera purpurea [Section 191h], a low bush with purple flowers with white centres.

plants.name: Platysace lanceolata
plants.context: On the left are several bushes of Platysace lanceolata [Section 191e] with white terminal clusters of flowers on an open bush.

plants.name: Banksia serrata
plants.context: Banksia serrata [Section 191e] also on the left is a small tree with very large greenish flowerheads, serrated leaves and a wrinkled trunk.

plants.name: Calytrix leschenaultii
plants.context: Calytrix leschenaultii [Section 14] is a delicate plant with pale mauve flowers with yellow centres.

plants.name: Halgania cyanea
plants.context: On the right is Halgania cyanea [Section 14] with bright blue flowers with dark centres on a tiny bush.

plants.name: Eremophila ionantha
plants.context: Eremophila ionantha [Section 14] from SW Western Australia is a small bush with narrow silvery-green leaves and mauve bell flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: We will visit the Red Centre Garden [Section 326] today. This garden has only recently been opened and is still under development. All the plants in this section grow in the dry inland area of central Australia.

plants.name: Solanum sturtianum
plants.context: As you enter the Red Centre Garden on the left is Solanum sturtianum, or Sturt’s Nightshade, with purple flowers with yellow anthers on an open bush of grey‑green foliage.

plants.name: Calandrinia balonensis
plants.context: Further on your left is Calandrinia balonensis, or Broad-leaf Parakeelya, a low bush with purple flowers on wiry stems.

plants.name: Acacia kempeana
plants.context: Bear left and on your right is Acacia kempeana, also called Witchetty Bush, a small bush with grey-green leaves and yellow rods of flower.

plants.name: Olearia stuartii
plants.context: On your left is Olearia stuartii, a small plant with mauve daisy flowers with yellow centres.

plants.name: Nicotiana rosulata subsp. ingulba
plants.context: Nicotiana rosulata subsp. ingulba, has a sharp scent, and white ‘tobacco’ flowers on lax foliage.

plants.name: Gossypium sturtianum
plants.context: Look to your right to see Gossypium sturtianum or Sturt’s Desert Rose, the floral emblem of the Northern Territory.

plants.name: Hibbertia glaberrima
plants.context: Hibbertia glaberrima on your left is a spreading shrub with bright yellow flowers.

plants.name: Cymbopogon obtectus
plants.context: On your right is Cymbopogon obtectus, or Silky Heads.

plants.name: Rhodanthe floribunda
plants.context: On your left Rhodanthe floribunda forms small mounds covered in masses of white flowers with gold centres.

plants.name: Sida calyxhymenia
plants.context: On your right is Sida calyxhymenia, or Tall Sida, an erect grey-leaved bush with small pale yellow flowers.

plants.name: Brachyscome iberidifolia
plants.context: On the left are several bushes of Brachyscome iberidifolia, the Swan River Daisy, with ferny foliage and bright purple almost iridescent flowers.

plants.name: Swainsona formosa
plants.context: Swainsona formosa or Sturt’s Desert Pea, also on the left, is the iconic shiny red and black flower of central Australia pictured at the top of this sheet.

plants.name: Eremophila willsii subsp. integrifolia
plants.context: Eremophila willsii subsp. integrifolia is a spindly shrub with mauve tubular flowers.

plants.name: Ptilotus nobilis subsp. nobilis
plants.context: On the right is Ptilotus nobilis subsp. nobilis with pale mauve feathery flowers on a neat small bush of hard leathery leaves.

plants.name: Rutidosis helichrysoides subsp. helichrysoides
plants.context: Rutidosis helichrysoides subsp. helichrysoides or Grey Wrinklewort is an erect branched herb with yellow globular heads of flower.

plants.name: Solanum orbiculatum subsp. orbiculatum
plants.context: Solanum orbiculatum subsp. orbiculatum on your left is a small, neat bush with purple ‘potato’ flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Today we start at the café and walk around the Main Path.

plants.name: Correa alba
plants.context: Just outside the café on the left is a medium-sized bush of Correa alba [Section 131] with grey-green leaves and white star flowers.

plants.name: Syzygium australe
plants.context: Nearby is a large bush of Syzygium australe [Section 131] with fluffy white flowers and red drooping fruit.

plants.name: Correa 'Summer Belle'
plants.context: Further along the path on the right is Correa ‘Summer Belle’ [Section 240] with pink bells with greenish tips.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia var. ericifolia
plants.context: On the left is Banksia ericifolia var. ericifolia [Section 30] with green developing flower-heads which mature into long gold candles on bright green heath-like foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea phanerophlebia
plants.context: Just around the next corner on your right is Grevillea phanerophlebia [Section 27], or Prominent Vein Grevillea, with white starburst terminal flowers on an airy bush.

plants.name: Callistemon 'Reeve's Pink'
plants.context: A little further on and to the left is Callistemon ‘Reeve’s Pink’ [Section 30] with bright pink brush-like flowers in profusion.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Coconut Ice'
plants.context: Just before crossing the road look to the right for Grevillea ‘Coconut Ice’ [Section 25], with large pink/orange spider flowers with long red styles.

plants.name: Banksia marginata 'Cape Patterson Dwarf'
plants.context: On the far side of the road is Banksia marginata ‘Cape Patterson Dwarf’ [Section 26] on the right is an unusual small version of our common local Banksia marginata.

plants.name: Banksia marginata
plants.context: On the far side of the road is Banksia marginata ‘Cape Patterson Dwarf’ [Section 26] on the right is an unusual small version of our common local Banksia marginata.

plants.name: Persoonia acerosa
plants.context: Just a little further on and to your right is Persoonia acerosa [Section 26], or Needle Geebung.

plants.name: Correa 'Marian's Marvel'
plants.context: On the right after crossing the next road is Correa ‘Marian’s Marvel’ [Section 112] with flared pale pink bells with greenish tips.

plants.name: Acacia linifolia
plants.context: On the left is Acacia linifolia [Section 191e], a small tree with sweetly-scented pale yellow balls on fine needle-like foliage.

plants.name: Podolobium aciculiferum
plants.context: After crossing the Eucalypt Lawn, on the left is Podolobium aciculiferum [Section 18] with long-lasting yellow pea flowers on spiky triangular foliage.

plants.name: Acacia subulata
plants.context: Further on the left is Acacia subulata [Section 18], or Awl-leaf Wattle, with airy fine foliage and scented yellow balls of flower for long periods of time.

plants.name: Acacia parvipinnula
plants.context: Look up on your left to see Acacia parvipinnula [Section 18], or Silver-stemmed Wattle, which is a tree of ferny foliage and yellow balls of flower.

plants.name: Epacris longiflora
plants.context: On your right is Epacris longiflora [Section 110], or Fuchsia Heath, showing red tubular flowers with white tips on a spiky bush of close foliage.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Today we will walk around the Rock Garden. Either follow the road up the hill past the back of the café or follow the Main Path through the Rainforest Gully to the Rock Garden.

plants.name: Grevillea lanigera
plants.context: As you enter the Rock Garden, on your left is Grevillea lanigera [Section 15c], a low bush with grey-green foliage and pink and cream flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Poorinda Royal Mantle'
plants.context: Further along the path on the right is Grevillea ‘Poorinda Royal Mantle’ [Section 15d], a fast-growing and vigorous groundcover with bright red toothbrush flowers.

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia
plants.context: On the left is Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia [Section 15c], another vigorous groundcover with dark green leaves that have attractive silver undersides.

plants.name: Correa 'Ivory Bells'
plants.context: On your right is Correa ‘Ivory Bells’ [Section 15d], a very floriferous plant with small dark green leaves and ivory tubular flowers.

plants.name: Chrysocephalum apiculatum
plants.context: Also on your right is Chrysocephalum apiculatum [Section 15d] with deep gold button flowers on a small bush of dark green foliage.

plants.name: Hibbertia serpyllifolia
plants.context: On the right Hibbertia serpyllifolia [Section 15f] has bright gold flowers on fine mid-green foliage.

plants.name: Olearia ramulosa var. stricta
plants.context: As you turn right, look up the path to your left to see Olearia ramulosa var. stricta [Section 15g] on the left, a small slight bush with plenty of white flowers.

plants.name: Philotheca linearis
plants.context: On the left just before you cross the plank bridge is Philotheca linearis [Section 15g], with small white fragrant 5-petalled star flowers with pink centres.

plants.name: Hibbertia vestita
plants.context: Turn right after the plank bridge and on the left is Hibbertia vestita [Section 15l], with flat yellow flowers on tiny foliage.

plants.name: Acacia aneura var. aneura
plants.context: Further along on the left is Acacia aneura var. aneura [Section 15l], an open bush with needle-like foliage and short fluffy yellow rods of flowers.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Birthday Candles'
plants.context: Turn left and on your left is Banksia spinulosa ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 15l], a dense bright green bush with attractive needle foliage and short yellow flower heads with rusty red styles.

plants.name: Verticordia pennigera
plants.context: Turn right down the hill and on your left is a pot of Verticordia pennigera [Section 15r], showing bright pink terminal clusters of fringed flowers on tiny grey-green foliage.

plants.name: Alyogyne 'West Coast Gem'
plants.context: On your left is Alyogyne ‘West Coast Gem’ [Section 15r] with clear purple ‘hibiscus’-like flowers which open for a short period only but are prolific.

plants.name: Eremophila bignoniiflora × E. polyclada
plants.context: On your left is Eremophila bignoniiflora x E. polyclada [Section 15r] with floppy linear foliage and large tubular lilac-tinged white flowers with spotted throats.

plants.name: Callistemon comboynensis
plants.context: Turn left along the road to see up to your left the Cliff Bottlebrush, Callistemon comboynensis [Section 15r], in full bloom with prominent red brushes on an upright bush.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: We will walk part of the Main Path today, starting amongst the eye-catching pots at the Visitor Information Centre (VIC).

plants.name: Hemiandra pungens
plants.context: Notice at the front of the VIC a pot of Hemiandra pungens [Section 221], commonly known as Snakebush, a trailing plant with bright green leaves and mauve tubular flowers.

plants.name: Lechenaultia formosa
plants.context: Also near the door is a pot of Lechenaultia formosa [Section 221] which is a small attractive plant with close grey-green foliage and bright red flowers with orange centres.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Birthday Candles'
plants.context: Further along on your right is Banksia spinulosa ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 174], a low shrub with needle-like foliage and yellow candle-like flower heads.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa var. spinulosa
plants.context: ‘Birthday Candles’ is a dwarf cultivar of Banksia spinulosa var. spinulosa developed by Bill Molyneux of Austraflora Nurseries in Montrose, Victoria.

plants.name: Banksia heliantha
plants.context: Banksia heliantha [Section 174], which used to be known as Oak-leaved Dryandra before the reclassification of all dryandras to banksias, is in a pot on your right.

plants.name: Spyridium burragorang
plants.context: Also on your right is Spyridium burragorang [Section 174], a long-flowering medium-sized shrub with unusual white bracts surrounding a central cluster of flowers.

plants.name: Correa 'Summer Belle'
plants.context: Cross the bridge and continue around the side of the café to see on your right Correa ‘Summer Belle’ [Section 240], which is a long-flowering small shrub with long pink bell flowers with protruding stamens.

plants.name: Epacris longiflora 'Nectar Pink'
plants.context: On your left is Epacris longiflora ‘Nectar Pink’ [Section 131], which is a very floriferous small shrub covered in slender pink bell flowers with white tips.

plants.name: Callistemon citrinus 'Splendens'
plants.context: Callistemon citrinus ‘Splendens’ [Section 240] is a small tree on your right with weeping foliage and bright red brush-like flowers beloved by spinebills and wattlebirds.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia subsp. ericifolia
plants.context: This is Banksia ericifolia subsp. ericifolia [Section 30] or Heath-leaved Banksia.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Honeypots'
plants.context: Further along on your right is another banksia in bloom, Banksia spinulosa ‘Honeypots’ [Section 9], a small bush with fine-toothed foliage and long orange flower heads.

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia
plants.context: Also on your right is Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia [Section 9], a large vigorous mounding groundcover with dark green leaves with silver backs and plenty of short greenish-yellow flower heads.

plants.name: Buckinghamia celsissima
plants.context: On your right is Buckinghamia celsissima [Section 27] or Ivory Curl, which is a small tree with fragrant dense terminal clusters of cylindrical ivory flower spikes.

plants.name: Hakea cycloptera
plants.context: Cross the road to see on your left Hakea cycloptera [Section 24], or Elm-seed Hakea, with incredibly prickly foliage and dusty pink flowers at the base of the leaves.

plants.name: Banksia marginata 'Cape Patterson Dwarf'
plants.context: Banksia marginata ‘Cape Patterson Dwarf’ [Section 26] on the right is an unusual small version of our common local Banksia marginata.

plants.name: Banksia conferta subsp. penicillata
plants.context: This lovely tree is Banksia conferta subsp. penicillata [Section 26] or Newnes Plateau Banksia.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: We will look for banksias in flower today which brighten up autumn in the Gardens.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Birthday Candles'
plants.context: On your right as you leave the VIC and reach the statue of Joseph Banks, for whom banksias are named, is Banksia spinulosa ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 174], a low shrub with needle-like foliage and yellow flower heads.

plants.context: ‘Birthday Candles’ is a dwarf cultivar of Banksia spinulosa var. spinulosa developed by Bill Molyneux of Austraflora Nurseries in Montrose, Victoria.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia subsp. ericifolia
plants.context: Rejoin the Main Path to see on your left Banksia ericifolia subsp. ericifolia [Section 30] or Heath-leaved Banksia, with finer foliage and smaller flower heads than B.

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia (prostrate form)
plants.context: On your right is Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia (prostrate form) [Section 9], or Coast Banksia.

plants.context: On your left is Banksia spinulosa var. neoanglica [Section 25] which is a compact medium-sized bush with grey-green foliage and bright yellow flower heads.

plants.name: Banksia paludosa
plants.context: Banksia paludosa [Section 27] is a small, upright tree on your right with upward-facing foliage and long greenish flower heads.

plants.name: Banksia blechnifolia
plants.context: Look down on your left to see Banksia blechnifolia [Section 25], a groundcover with fishbone foliage and deep reddish-brown flower heads emerging at the base.

plants.name: Banksia oblongifolia
plants.context: This is Banksia oblongifolia [Section 25].

plants.name: Banksia marginata 'Cape Patterson Dwarf'
plants.context: Banksia marginata ‘Cape Patterson Dwarf’ [Section 26] on the right is an unusual small version of our common local Banksia marginata.

plants.name: Banksia conferta subsp. pencillata
plants.context: This lovely tree is Banksia conferta subsp. pencillata [Section 26] or Newnes Plateau Banksia.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia 'Red Clusters'
plants.context: On your left is Banksia ericifolia ‘Red Clusters’ [Section 26], a shrub or small tree with yellow flower heads aging to rusty red.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa var. cunninghamii
plants.context: Turn left up the road to see on your right Banksia spinulosa var. cunninghamii [Section 191e] or Hairpin Banksia, which is a small tree with yellow flower heads and prominent black styles.

plants.name: Banksia aemula
plants.context: Further on your right behind the log seat is the Wallum Banksia or Banksia aemula [Section 191l] with upright toothed foliage and a mixture of immature and mature flower heads.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Honey Pots'
plants.context: Here on your left is Banksia spinulosa ‘Honey Pots’ [Section 15d], a medium-sized bush with yellow flower heads.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens

plants.name: Lechenaultia formosa

plants.name: Epacris impressa

plants.name: Prostanthera phylicifolia
plants.context: Prostanthera phylicifolia [Section 210], or Spiked Mint-bush, has masses of small mauve flowers on a lax bush which scrambles down a bank.

plants.name: Epacris longiflora 'Nectar Pink'

plants.context: In a pot on your left is Grevillea saccata [Section 30] a shrub with terminal clusters of reddish‑orange flowers that have prominent yellow pouches housing the anthers.

plants.context: On your left is Callistemon ‘Reeve’s Pink’ [Section 30], a medium bush with bright pink brush-like flowers much loved by bees.

plants.context: Cross the road to see on your left Hakea cycloptera [Section 24], or Elm-seed Hakea, with pale pink curled flowers on spiky needle-like foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea centristigma
plants.context: On your right is the unusual Grevillea centristigma [Section 26], a small bush with soft lush foliage fringed with white hairs.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: We will walk to the Rock Garden today, first taking the path at the rear of the café.

plants.context: On you right is the standard grevillea Grevillea bipinnatifida ‘Jingle Bells’ [Section 124], with stiff, prickly, divided foliage and orange-red racemes of flowers.

plants.context: Further on your right is a small tree with fine linear foliage, Banksia spinulosa var. spinulosa [Section 109], with pale yellow flowers with styles that turn rusty red as they mature.

plants.name: Acronychyia littoralis
plants.context: On your left is Acronychyia littoralis[Section 114], a small rainforest tree with beautiful shiny leaves and creamy white scented clusters of flower.

plants.name: Grevillea lanigera
plants.context: Enter up the steps to your left to see Grevillea lanigera [Section 15c], a low bush or groundcover of grey-green close foliage with pink and cream flowers.

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia
plants.context: Also on your left is Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia [Section 15c] or Coast Banksia, a scrambling mass of dark green silver-backed foliage and plenty of yellow upright flower heads.

plants.name: Correa 'Ivory Bells'
plants.context: On your right is Correa ‘Ivory Bells’ [Section 15d], with dark green foliage and masses of cream bell flowers that are much loved by birds and bees.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Honey Pots'
plants.context: Also on your right is Banksia spinulosa ‘Honey Pots’ [Section 15d], a neat compact mid-sized shrub with fine silver-backed linear foliage and orange flower heads with rusty red styles.
