title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: A walk along the curvaceous Main Path from the Visitor Centre towards the Eucalyptus Lawn, Red Centre Garden and Sydney Region Flora section.

plants.name: Lechenaultia formosa
plants.context: Near the Visitor Centre door, Lechenaultia formosa [Section 221] is a small attractive plant from WA, with close, grey-green foliage and bright red flowers with orange centres.

plants.name: Hibbertia vestita
plants.context: On the left, behind the bright yellow flowers of Hibbertia vestita, is Prostanthera phylicifolia[Section 210] which has masses of mauve flowers and aromatic foliage.

plants.name: Prostanthera phylicifolia
plants.context: On the left, behind the bright yellow flowers of Hibbertia vestita, is Prostanthera phylicifolia[Section 210] which has masses of mauve flowers and aromatic foliage.

plants.name: Olearia argophylla
plants.context: At the Café bridge, on the left, is Olearia argophylla [Section 305], known as ‘Native Musk’.

plants.name: Correa baeuerlenii
plants.context: On the left, near the door to the Ellis Rowan Building, is Correa baeuerlenii [Section 131], or Chef’s Hat Correa.

plants.name: Crowea 'Cooper's Hybrid'
plants.context: Further on the right beneath a Brittle Gum tree (Eucalyptus mannifera), is Crowea ‘Cooper’s Hybrid’ [Section 240], with pink, star-shaped flowers.

plants.name: Acacia alata var. biglandulosa
plants.context: Acacia alata var. biglandulosa [Section 240], the Winged Wattle from WA, has a profusion of small, cream, ball-shaped flowers attached to unusual zig-zag stems.

plants.name: Thryptomene
plants.context: Continue along the Main Path to a large bush of a Thryptomene species [Section 10] on the left; this has tiny, dainty, open-petalled, pink flowers, in clusters.

plants.name: Melaleuca fulgens 'Hot Pink'
plants.context: Further on the left, behind the Melaleuca fulgens ‘Hot Pink’ is Callistemon subulatus [Section 10], with bright, red flower spikes.

plants.name: Callistemon subulatus
plants.context: Further on the left, behind the Melaleuca fulgens ‘Hot Pink’ is Callistemon subulatus [Section 10], with bright, red flower spikes.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia subsp. ericifolia
plants.context: Continue along the Main Path to the Proteaceae Section and find on the left Banksia ericifolia subsp. ericifolia [Section 30], Heath Banksia, with glowing orange flower spikes when mature.

plants.name: Banksia heliantha
plants.context: On the right is Banksia heliantha [Section 30] from WA, previously known as Dryandra quercifolia before reclassification as a banksia.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Birthday Candles'
plants.context: Nearby on the left, is Banksia spinulosa ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 30], a low shrub with needle-like foliage, and yellow flower heads.

plants.name: Birthday Candles'
plants.context: Nearby on the left, is Banksia spinulosa ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 30], a low shrub with needle-like foliage, and yellow flower heads.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Coconut Ice'
plants.context: Before crossing the road, on the right, is Grevillea ‘Coconut Ice’, with spectacular, large, orange-pink sprays of flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea centristigma
plants.context: Over the road and further along the Main Path, on the right, is a small bush of Grevillea centristigma [Section 25], with bright yellow flowers and orange stamens.

plants.name: Grevillea phanerophlebia
plants.context: Further along, on the left, is Grevillea phanerophlebia [Section 24], a large shrub, with delicate, white, feathery flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea ripicola
plants.context: Just before the road, also on the left, is a large, sprawling shrub of Grevillea ripicola [Section 24], with red and gold spider-like flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: This walk commences on the Main Path, just past the café outside the Ellis Rowan Building. It then continues uphill past the Red Centre Garden to the Western Mallee section. Wonderful flowers and lovely views.

plants.name: Banksia 'Stumpy Gold'
plants.context: Near the entrance to the Ellis Rowan Building is the low-growing Banksia ‘Stumpy Gold’ [Section 131] with developing flower spikes, open flowers and mature cones.

plants.name: Crowea 'Cooper's Hybrid'
plants.context: Further along on the right you will see Crowea ‘Cooper’s Hybrid’ [Section 240], a delightful plant in winter with its pink star-shaped flowers.

plants.name: Thryptomene saxicola 'Pink Lace'
plants.context: On the right just past the aging Eucalyptus mannifera admire the lacy foliage and tiny pink flowers of Thryptomene saxicola ‘Pink Lace’ [Section10], a low spreading shrub.

plants.name: Epacris longiflora
plants.context: On the left-hand side near the top of the road is Epacris longiflora [Section 110], with delightful red tubular flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea lanigera
plants.context: At the first step is Grevillea lanigera [Section 15c].

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia
plants.context: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia [Section 15c], the Coast Banksia, spills down the steps displaying its yellow flower heads.

plants.name: Correa 'Ivory Bells'
plants.context: On the right is Correa ‘Ivory Bells’ [Section 15d], covered with bell-shaped creamy flowers.

plants.name: Acacia pterocaulon
plants.context: In a pot ahead you can see the first yellow globular inflorescences of Acacia pterocaulon [Section 15e] displayed on its unusual branchlets.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa 'Birthday Candles'
plants.context: Turn right and before you leave the Rock Garden you will see Banksia spinulosa ‘Birthday Candles’ [Section 15l], bearing golden flower heads with prominent red styles.

plants.name: Nicotiana rosulata subsp. ingulba
plants.context: Nicotiana rosulata subsp. ingulba [Section 326] has white flowers and is used by some indigenous Australians as a type of tobacco.

plants.name: Swainsona formosa
plants.context: Look also for the red flowers of Sturt’s Desert Pea, Swainsona formosa.

plants.name: Astartea sp
plants.context: The tiny pink flowers and delicate leaves of an Astartea sp. [Section 100c] greet you.

plants.name: Hakea cycloptera
plants.context: Hakea cycloptera [Section 100c] holds spidery pink flower heads close to its branches.

plants.name: Acacia alata var. biglandulosa
plants.context: Acacia alata var. biglandulosa [Section 100c] displays flattened zigzag phyllodes and fluffy cream flower heads.

plants.name: Acacia aphylla
plants.context: Look to the right and you will see Acacia aphylla [Section 100a], with its yellow flower heads on the wiry leafless branches.

plants.name: Banksia epica
plants.context: Banksia epica [Section 100a] has lime buds and creamy yellow mature flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: We will stick closely to the Visitors Information Centre area this week and concentrate on the flowers in pots and the endangered plant area. You do not have to walk far in the Gardens to see interesting and beautiful plants in flower.

plants.name: Lechenaultia formosa
plants.context: Lechenaultia formosa [Section 221] in a pot on the right is a small attractive plant with close grey-green foliage and bright red flowers with orange centres.

plants.name: Hemiandra pungens
plants.context: Hemiandra pungens [Section 221], also in a pot on the right and commonly known as Snakebush, is a trailing plant with bright green leaves and mauve tubular flowers which is endemic to south-western Western Australia where it grows on rocky outcrops.

plants.name: Brachyscome tatei
plants.context: Brachyscome tatei [Section 221] in the same pot area is considered rare in the wild.

plants.name: Anigozanthos hybrid 'Bush Volcano'
plants.context: Follow the path and past the Joseph Banks bust on your right in a pot is Anigozanthos hybrid ‘Bush Volcano’ [Section 174], which has long lasting rusty-red paw flowers.

plants.name: Banksia heliantha
plants.context: Banksia heliantha [Section 174], which used to be known as Oak-leaved Dryandra before the reclassification of all dryandras to banksias, is in a pot on your right.

plants.name: Spyridium burragorang
plants.context: Spyridium burragorang [Section 174], on your right is a long-flowering, medium-sized shrub with unusual white bracts surrounding a central pinkish-brown cluster of flowers.

plants.name: Epacris longiflora
plants.context: Epacris longiflora [Section 174] on your right has long thin tube-like white flowers on a straggly light green bush.

plants.name: Grevillea rosmarinifolia 'Scarlet Sprite'
plants.context: Grevillea rosmarinifolia ‘Scarlet Sprite’ [Section 174] on your right is just coming into bloom with bright red clusters of flowers on a neat bush of fine green foliage.

plants.name: Woollsia pungens
plants.context: Also on your right is Woollsia pungens [Section 174], a straggly light green bush with terminal white flower heads which have a strong scent.

plants.name: Epacris impressa
plants.context: Continuing on your right is Epacris impressa [Section 174], another straggly bush with bright pink tubular flowers.

plants.name: Prostanthera phylicifolia
plants.context: Prostanthera phylicifolia [Section 210], or Spiked Mint-bush, on your left has masses of small mauve flowers on a lax bush which scrambles down a bank.

plants.name: Zieria formosa
plants.context: Continue around the corner to your right to see Zieria formosa [Section 174], or Shapely Zieria, with soft grey foliage contrasting harmoniously with the small light pink clusters of flowers.

plants.name: Thryptomene saxicola
plants.context: Thryptomene saxicola [Section 174] makes a strong display with airy arching sprays of tiny pink flowers on fine green foliage.

plants.name: Allocasuarina littoralis
plants.context: At the base of the steps you will find Allocasuarina littoralis [Section 174] with fluffy red blooms on a sparse tree with many cones remaining on the branches.

plants.name: Myoporum turbinatum
plants.context: Myoporum turbinatum [Section 221] on the left of the steps has tiny white star flowers in high contrast to the dark linear foliage.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Today we will walk along the Main Path between the café and the beginning of the Sydney Region Gully. There are plenty of plants in flower, even in the middle of winter.

plants.name: Banksia 'Stumpy Gold'
plants.context: Banksia ‘Stumpy Gold’ [Section 131] on your left is a neat low bush with many golden flowers.

plants.name: Eucalyptus gregsoniana
plants.context: Eucalyptus gregsoniana [Section 131], also known as the Wolgan Snow Gum, is a mallee that is found in the highlands of New South Wales.

plants.name: Epacris longiflora
plants.context: Epacris longiflora [Section 131], or Native Fuchsia, on your left, has thin tubular white-tipped red flowers on a small prickly bush.

plants.name: Epacris longiflora 'Nectar Pink'
plants.context: Epacris longiflora ‘Nectar Pink’ [Section 131], also on your left, is a selection from the above species.

plants.name: Acacia alata var. biglandulosa
plants.context: Acacia alata var. biglandulosa [Section 240], or Winged Wattle, on the right, has flattened phyllodes and masses of white fluffy ball flowers.

plants.name: Thryptomene sp
plants.context: A Thryptomene sp. [Section 10] on your left is an airy bush with a graceful, arching habit and close neat foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea speciosa
plants.context: Grevillea speciosa [Section 30] on the left, also known as Red Spider Flower, is a shrub which is endemic to New South Wales.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia subsp. ericifolia
plants.context: Banksia ericifolia subsp. ericifolia [Section 30], on your left, is a long-flowering, medium-sized shrub with attractive divided foliage and long orange inflorescences.

plants.name: Grevillea diminuta
plants.context: Grevillea diminuta [Section 30] on your left has hanging clusters of orange/red flowers on a neat medium-sized bush.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa var. neoanglica
plants.context: Banksia spinulosa var. neoanglica [Section 7], or New England Banksia, on your left, has silver-backed dark green foliage with glorious yellow/gold brushes held upright.

plants.name: Banksia marginata 'Cape Patterson Dwarf'
plants.context: Banksia marginata ‘Cape Patterson Dwarf’ [Section 26], across the road on the right, is an unusual small version of our common local Banksia marginata.

plants.name: Grevillea centristigma
plants.context: Also on your right is Grevillea centristigma [Section 26], a small bush with soft lush foliage fringed with white hairs.

plants.name: Grevillea manglesii subsp. ornithopoda
plants.context: Grevillea manglesii subsp. ornithopoda [Section 24], or Birdsfoot Grevillea, on the left, is a large open bush with pincushion-like white flower heads all along the stems.

plants.name: Grevillea vestita subsp. isopogoides
plants.context: Continuing on your right is Grevillea vestita subsp. isopogoides [Section 26], a spreading, prostrate, prickly bush with masses of white starburst flowers native to Western Australia.

plants.name: Phebalium squamulosum
plants.context: Phebalium squamulosum [Section 112], on your left, is a small bush with yellow star flowers with prominent stamens.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Let’s walk to the Rock Garden today to see what is in flower there on a cool winter’s day.

plants.name: Olearia argophylla
plants.context: Olearia argophylla [Section 305], or Native Musk, on your right is a tall shrub or small tree with felted grey leaves and white, strongly-scented flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea rosmarinifolia 'Rosy Posy'
plants.context: Grevillea rosmarinifolia ‘Rosy Posy’ [Section 128] on your right is a compact bush with linear foliage and pendent racemes of pink and cream flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Goldfever'
plants.context: Grevillea ‘Goldfever’ [Section 124], again on your right, is a low spreading shrub that produces golden flowers for most of the year.

plants.name: Grevillea lanigera
plants.context: Go up the steps to your left to notice on the left-hand side Grevillea lanigera [Section 15c] with grey-green foliage and pink and cream flowers on a low bush.

plants.name: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia
plants.context: Banksia integrifolia subsp. integrifolia [Section 15c], also on your left, is a vigorous groundcover with dark green leaves that have attractive silver backs.

plants.name: Grevillea manglesii subsp. ornithopoda
plants.context: Grevillea manglesii subsp. ornithopoda [Section 15d], or Birdsfoot Grevillea, on your right, is a large open bush with divided foliage and white pincushion flower heads all along the stems.

plants.name: Acacia pterocaulon
plants.context: Acacia pterocaulon [Section 15e] on the right in a pot, just coming into flower, is a much-branched, intricate shrub with very large golden ball flowers and flattened foliage.

plants.name: Androcalva luteiflora
plants.context: Androcalva luteiflora [Section 15f], on your right is a rounded bush with small round foliage and yellow cup flowers with red centres.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Little Jessie'
plants.context: Grevillea ‘Little Jessie’ [Section 15g], up to your right, is a hybrid between Grevillea asparagoides and G.calliantha.

plants.name: Grevillea iaspicula
plants.context: Grevillea iaspicula [Section 15h] on your left, also known as the Wee Jasper Grevillea, is an endangered shrub that is endemic to southern New South Wales.

plants.name: Commersonia magniflora
plants.context: Commersonia magniflora [Section 15g], high on your right, grows in central and western Australia.

plants.name: Acacia alata var. platyptera
plants.context: Acacia alata var. platyptera [Section 15f] on your right has bipinnate flattened phyllodes and very large golden ball flowers.

plants.name: Hakea obtusa
plants.context: Cross the plank bridge and turn right down the hill to see Hakea obtusa [Section 15p] on your left, a small tree with leathery foliage and dark pink powderpuff flowers along the stems.

plants.name: Alyogyne huegelii 'West Coast Gem'
plants.context: Go to the bottom of the steps near the waterfall and then turn left up the other set of steps to see Alyogyne huegelii ‘West Coast Gem’ [Section 15r], on your right with clear purple ‘hibiscus’ flowers.

plants.name: Hakea corymbosa
plants.context: Further up on your left is Hakea corymbosa [Section 15p], or Cauliflower Hakea, a small tree with incredibly prickly foliage and greenish cream flowers in bunches.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Take a walk along the road behind the café and up the hill to see many plants in flower, including the early flowering wattles.

plants.name: Acacia podalyriifolia
plants.context: Acacia podalyriifolia [Section 126], or Queensland Silver Wattle, on the right, has large golden balls of flowers on attractive grey-green foliage.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa
plants.context: Banksia spinulosa [Section 126], on your right, has large golden flowerheads held upright on toothed linear grey-green foliage.

plants.name: Westringia eremicola
plants.context: Westringia eremicola [Section 126], or Slender Westringia, again on your right, has grey-green linear foliage with pale mauve flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Poorinda Diadem'
plants.context: On your right-hand side, Grevillea ‘Poorinda Diadem’ [Section 126] is a tall straggly bush with many butterscotch-yellow flowers with long styles.

plants.name: Eremophila microtheca
plants.context: Eremophila microtheca [Section 302], also on your right, is a wispy grey-foliaged bush with mauve tubular flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea aspleniifolia
plants.context: Grevillea aspleniifolia [Section 124], on your left, is a very large sprawling shrub with long linear toothed green foliage and red toothbrush flowers.

plants.name: Leucopogon melaleucoides
plants.context: Leucopogon melaleucoides [Section 110] is a small neat bush with dark green foliage and clusters of terminal white flowers.

plants.name: Guichenotia ledifolia
plants.context: Turn right along the Main Path to see on your right Guichenotia ledifolia [Section 4], with grey-green foliage covered in masses of dusty pink 5-petalled flowers with maroon centres.

plants.name: Kunzea pulchella
plants.context: Kunzea pulchella [Section 15r], on your left, is a medium-sized bush with grey-green foliage and spectacular bright red “bottlebrush” flowers.

plants.name: Thryptomene sp
plants.context: A Thryptomene sp. [Section 14] on your left is an airy bush with a graceful, arching habit covered in clusters of tiny pink flowers with darker centres on close neat foliage.

plants.name: Acacia amoena
plants.context: Acacia amoena [Section 3], or Boomerang Wattle, on your right, is a small bush with tough yellow-green leaves and golden balls of flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea monticola
plants.context: Grevillea monticola [Section 14], on your left, has spiky “holly-like” foliage with many rusty orange buds which open to small white toothbrush flowers.

plants.name: Acacia 'Purpurea'
plants.context: Acacia ‘Purpurea’ [Section 3] on your right has many sprays of golden ball flowers and striking silver-grey fringed foliage with a feathery texture.

plants.name: Homoranthus cernuus
plants.context: Homoranthus cernuus [Section 15j], on your left, has tight grey foliage with prominent red buds in twos and threes that open to a cream flower with long exserted stamens.

plants.name: Grevillea iaspicula
plants.context: Grevillea iaspicula [Section 15h], on your left, also known as Wee Jasper Grevillea, is an endangered shrub that is endemic to southern New South Wales.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Let us concentrate on our wonderful wattles today.

plants.name: Acacia gordonii
plants.context: Walk along the path from the VIC to see on your right Acacia gordonii [Section 174], a small neat bush with bright gold balls of flowers.

plants.name: Acacia myrtifolia
plants.context: Acacia myrtifolia [Section 174], further along on your right, is an interesting and unusual wattle that has bright red new growth and stems with green elliptical phyllodes and cream balls of flowers.

plants.name: Acacia filicifolia
plants.context: Acacia filicifolia [Section 2] or Fern-leaf Wattle], on your left, has dark green ferny foliage and masses of bright yellow balls of flowers. It occurs naturally in southern Queensland and New South Wales. Also on your left hand side is Acacia kybeanensis [Section 2], a medium shrub with grey-green foliage and yellow balls of flowers. plants.name: Acacia kybeanensis
plants.context: Also on your left hand side is Acacia kybeanensis [Section 2], a medium shrub with grey-green foliage and yellow balls of flowers.

plants.name: Acacia 'Purpurea'
plants.context: Acacia ‘Purpurea’ [Section 3], on your left, has many sprays of golden flowers with striking silver-grey fringed foliage with a feathery texture.

plants.name: Acacia baileyana
plants.context: This showy form of Acacia baileyana is very fast-growing and tough.

plants.name: Acacia amoena
plants.context: Acacia amoena [Section 3], or Boomerang Wattle, on your left, is a small bush with tough yellow-green leaves and golden balls of flowers.

plants.name: Acacia phlebophylla
plants.context: On your left behind the previous plant is Acacia phlebophylla [Section 3].

plants.name: Acacia colletioides
plants.context: In front of the previous plant is Acacia colletioides [Section 3], a very prickly sprawling shrub with fine linear foliage and small golden balls of flowers.

plants.name: Acacia covenyi
plants.context: Acacia covenyi [Section 3], commonly known as Blue Bush, up the road on your left has magnificent silver grey foliage and masses of contrasting bright gold flower balls.

plants.name: Acacia ingramii
plants.context: Acacia ingramii [Section 3] on your left is a large bush or small tree with fine linear foliage and masses of gold flower balls.

plants.name: Acacia guinetii
plants.context: Acacia guinetii [Section 18], or Golden Gravel Wattle, on your left, has a compact shape and soft grey-green foliage with many gold flower balls.

plants.name: Acacia cardiophylla
plants.context: Acacia cardiophylla [Section 18], or West Wyalong Wattle, on your left, has ferny light green bipinnate foliage and masses of yellow balls of flowers.

plants.name: Acacia meiantha
plants.context: Acacia meiantha [Section 18] on your left, is a small straggling shrub with very fine needle foliage and masses of small yellow flower balls.

plants.name: Acacia aphylla
plants.context: Acacia aphylla [Section 18], or Leafless Rock Wattle, on the left, has large gold balls of flowers on leathery leafless stems.

plants.name: Acacia brunioides subsp. brunioides
plants.context: Acacia brunioides subsp. brunioides [Section 18] or Brown Wattle on your left is a small light bush with cream balls of flowers on bright green foliage.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: A short walk from the VIC will find many spring-flowering plants in bloom throughout the Gardens at this time.

plants.name: Acacia gordonii
plants.context: Acacia gordonii [Section 174], on the right, is a small neat bush with bright gold balls of flowers.

plants.name: Chorizema cordatum
plants.context: Chorizema cordatum [Section 174] or Heart-leaved Flame Pea, on the right in a pot, is a showy weeping shrub with vivid red flowers and bright green prickly foliage.

plants.name: Acacia myrtifolia
plants.context: Acacia myrtifolia [Section 174], further along on your right, is an interesting and unusual wattle that has vibrant red new growth and stems with green elliptical phyllodes and cream balls of flowers.

plants.name: Acacia melanoxylon
plants.context: As you walk across the bridge notice on your left a large tree, Acacia melanoxylon [Section 305], with many pale yellow balls of flowers and “eucalypt-like” phyllodes.

plants.name: Daviesia horrida
plants.context: As you walk past the café look to your left to see Daviesia horrida [Section 245] with extremely prickly grey foliage showing off bright orange/red pea flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea sericea subsp. sericea
plants.context: Also on your left is Grevillea sericea subsp. sericea [Section 244], an open, airy bush with light green foliage and white spider flowers.

plants.name: Eucalyptus gregsoniana
plants.context: In the Ellis Rowan Garden on your left [Section 131] is the mallee gum, Eucalyptus gregsoniana, with a grey trunk and white fluffy flowers.

plants.name: Alyogyne huegelii 'West Coast Gem'
plants.context: On your right is Alyogyne huegelii ‘West Coast Gem’ [Section 240], with clear purple “hibiscus” flowers and coarse divided foliage.

plants.name: Phebalium squamulosum subsp. lineare
plants.context: Also on the right is Phebalium squamulosum subsp. lineare [Section 240], a medium-sized bush with fine needle-like foliage and pale yellow flowers with prominent stamens.

plants.name: Micromyrtus ciliata
plants.context: Further on your left is Micromyrtus ciliata [Section 131] with graceful arching sprays of very fine close foliage and masses of tiny white flowers opening from pink buds.

plants.name: Acacia alata var. biglandulosa
plants.context: Acacia alata var. biglandulosa [Section 240], or Winged Wattle, on the right, has flattened phyllodes and masses of white fluffy balls of flowers.

plants.name: Homoranthus flavescens
plants.context: Continue straight ahead to see on your right‑hand side Homoranthus flavescens [Section 143], a neat bush with needle-like leaves and bright acid yellow flowers on top of the foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea rosmarinifolia
plants.context: Turn right and on your right is Grevillea rosmarinifolia [Section 180], with prickly grey-green needle foliage and bright pinkish-red flowers.

plants.name: Zieria formosa
plants.context: Also on your right is Zieria formosa [Section 180], with masses of dusty pink flowers with darker centres.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia var. ericifolia
plants.context: On the right is Banksia ericifolia var. ericifolia [Section 306] with bright orange flower heads and green “heath-like” foliage.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: The Gardens are full of spring flowers at this time. Feast your eyes in all directions.

plants.name: Rhodanthe chlorocephala
plants.context: Rhodanthe chlorocephala [Section 221; also pictured above] is on your right in a pot as you leave the Visitor Information Centre.

plants.name: Gastrolobium involutum
plants.context: Gastrolobium involutum [Section 221], also on the right in a pot, is an erect spreading shrub with linear leaves and orange pea flowers.

plants.name: Philotheca myoporoides subsp. acuta
plants.context: Philotheca myoporoides subsp. acuta [Section 174], on the right, is a neat bush with masses of pale pink flowers opening from darker pink buds.

plants.name: Acacia boormanii
plants.context: Acacia boormanii [Section 210], or Snowy River Wattle, on your left, has fine needle foliage and masses of golden balls of flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Scarlet Sprite'
plants.context: Grevillea ‘Scarlet Sprite’ [Section 174], on the right, is a cultivar of G.

plants.name: Chorizema cordatum
plants.context: Chorizema cordatum [Section 174] or Heart-leaved Flame Pea, on the right in a pot, is a showy weeping shrub with vivid red/orange flowers and bright green prickly foliage.

plants.name: Thelychiton speciosus
plants.context: Thelychiton speciosus [Section 125], on your left, is a popular and widely grown orchid previously known as Dendrobium speciosum.

plants.name: Leionema elatius subsp. beckleri
plants.context: Leionema elatius subsp. beckleri [Section 125], on your left, has shiny green leaves and clusters of scented white flowers.

plants.name: Chamelaucium 'Cascade Brook'
plants.context: On your right as you turn right along the bitumen road is Chamelaucium ‘Cascade Brook’ [Section 17], or Geraldton Wax.

plants.name: Chamelaucium uncinatum 'Murfit Rose'

plants.name: Prostanthera rotundifolia
plants.context: Prostanthera rotundifolia [Section 78] or Round-leaved Mint Bush, on your right, has deliciously-scented foliage and many purple flowers.

plants.name: Acacia pravissima 'Kuranga Cascade'
plants.context: On your right is Acacia pravissima ‘Kuranga Cascade’ [Section 15j], a weeping or prostrate wattle with triangular grey-green phyllodes and masses of golden balls of flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea monticola
plants.context: Also on the right is Grevillea monticola [Section 14], which has stiff, prickly, holly-like leaves covered with many clusters of cream flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea vestita
plants.context: Grevillea vestita [Section 20], on the right, is a large open bush with many starbursts of white flowers.

plants.name: Logania albiflora

plants.name: Zieria prostrata
plants.context: On the corner on your right is Zieria prostrata [Section 221], a multi-stemmed, prostrate, mat-forming shrub with pink star flowers in profusion.

plants.name: Prostanthera stricta
plants.context: Prostanthera stricta [Section 174], or Mount Vincent Mint Bush, on the left is a small bush with tiny aromatic leaves and violet flowers.

plants.name: Phebalium daviesii
plants.context: On the right is Phebalium daviesii [Section 221], or St.

plants.name: Hardenbergia violacea
plants.context: Hardenbergia violacea [Section 174], on your left, is a vigorous vine with oblong leathery leaves and bright purple pea flowers.

plants.name: Acacia alata var. alata
plants.context: Acacia alata var. alata [Section 174], or Winged Wattle, on the left has lemon balls of flowers on dark green flattened phyllodes.

plants.name: Acacia pubescens
plants.context: Acacia pubescens [Section 174], or Downy Wattle, on the left has gold balls of flowers on fringed foliage.

plants.name: Hibbertia empetrifolia
plants.context: Hibbertia empetrifolia [Section 174], on your left, has bright gold coin flowers on a small scrambling shrub.

plants.name: Gastrolobium celsianum
plants.context: Gastrolobium celsianum [Section 174], on your left, forms a low loose bush with bright red curved flowers.

plants.name: Tetratheca pilosa subsp. latifolia
plants.context: On your right in the small bed is Tetratheca pilosa subsp. latifolia [Section 174], a small bush with bright mauve flowers with darker centres.

plants.name: Richea dracophylla
plants.context: On your left is Richea dracophylla [Section 66], with creamy spires of flower and spiky foliage.

plants.name: Rhodanthe anthemoides
plants.context: On your right Rhodanthe anthemoides [Section 60], also known as Chamomile Sunray forms mounds of white daisies with prominent yellow centres.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Today we walk along part of the Main Path to be rewarded by many plants in flower.

plants.name: Chorizema cordatum
plants.context: As you leave the VIC look to your left to see in a pot the extravagant bloom of Chorizema cordatum [Section 221] or Heart-leaved Flame Pea.

plants.name: Alyogyne huegelii 'West Coast Gem'
plants.context: On your left is Alyogyne huegelii ‘West Coast Gem’ [Section 210], with clear purple ‘hibiscus’ style flowers which open for a short period only but are prolific.

plants.name: Hibbertia empetrifolia
plants.context: Also on your left is Hibbertia empetrifolia [Section 210] with masses of gold coin flowers on the wiry foliage.

plants.name: Richea dracophylla
plants.context: As you cross the bridge notice on your right Richea dracophylla [Section 66], with creamy spires of flower and spiky foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea sericea subsp. sericea
plants.context: Further on your left as you skirt the café is Grevillea sericea subsp. sericea [Section 244], or Silky Grevillea, an open bush with white frothy spider flowers.It is native to the central coast of NSW.

plants.name: Libertia paniculata
plants.context: On the left is Libertia paniculata [Section 131] with iris-like foliage and white branched flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Bonfire'
plants.context: As you veer right down towards the Crosbie Morrison building you see on your left a very large bush of Grevillea ‘Bonfire’ [Section 240], with bright red waxy blooms on dark green linear foliage.

plants.name: Philotheca myoporoides
plants.context: Philotheca myoporoides [Section 240] has masses of white flowers with pink buds.

plants.name: Isopogon anethifolius
plants.context: Isopogon anethifolius [Section 240] has vigorous upright linear foliage with bright yellow ‘drumstick’ flowers.

plants.name: Commersonia (Rulingia) magniflora
plants.context: Commersonia (Rulingia) magniflora [Section 240] on your left, has strongly scented white flowers with pink centres.

plants.name: Melaleuca fulgens 'Hot Pink'
plants.context: Go left up the stairs towards the Main Path and continue up the hill to see on your left Melaleuca fulgens ‘Hot Pink’ [Section 10], with attractive bottlebrush flowers that are hot pink with gold stamens.

plants.name: Bulbine glauca
plants.context: On your left are several Bulbine glauca [Section 8], with spires of lemon flowers opening sequentially.

plants.name: Doryanthes excelsa
plants.context: Look up to your left to see one of the most spectacular flowers in the Gardens Doryanthes excelsa [Section 8], or Gymea Lily, just beginning to open.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.context: Telopea speciosissima [Section 30] also on your left forms another spectacular display.

plants.name: Kunzea parvifolia
plants.context: On your left is Kunzea parvifolia [Section 30], a large bush with fluffy white flowers scented strongly with honey and much beloved by insects.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: There are so many plants in flower at this time that it is hard to choose which ones to feature.

plants.name: Dendrobium × delicatum
plants.context: As you leave the Visitor Information Centre look to your left to see Dendrobium × delicatum [Section 212], an orchid with clusters of white flowers and oblong green foliage.

plants.name: Gastrolobium involutum
plants.context: On your right in a pot is Gastrolobium involutum [Section 221], with bright orange/yellow pea flowers on graceful fine linear foliage.

plants.name: Swainsona formosa
plants.context: Further on your right in a pot is Swainsona formosa [Section 221], or Sturt’s Desert Pea, with pale green leaves and bright red pea flowers.

plants.name: Hibbertia stellaris
plants.context: Notice in a pot on your right Hibbertia stellaris [Section 174], or Orange Stars, with masses of orange star flowers on wiry foliage.

plants.name: Conostylis candicans subsp. candicans
plants.context: In a small bed on your right before crossing the bridge are clumps of Conostylis candicans subsp. candicans [Section 174], with yellow flower-heads on fine grey strappy foliage.

plants.name: Vesselowskya rubifolia
plants.context: Look high on your left to see Vesselowskya rubifolia [Section 210], a large shrub with serrated green leaves and fluffy racemes of pink and cream flowers.

plants.name: Olearia argophylla
plants.context: As you cross the bridge notice on your right Olearia argophylla [Section 66], a tall shrubby daisy with many white flower-heads with gold centres.

plants.name: Pimelea ferruginea 'Magenta Mist'
plants.context: Pimelea ferruginea ‘Magenta Mist’ [Section 131], on your left in the Ellis Rowan Garden, has bright pink flower-heads on neat foliage.

plants.name: Homoranthus flavescens
plants.context: On your right towards the top of the hill is Homoranthus flavescens [Section 9] with acid yellow blooms layered on a small bush.

plants.name: Melaleuca diosmifolia
plants.context: Melaleuca diosmifolia [Section 9], on your right, has green brush-like flowers on neat darker green foliage.

plants.name: Doryanthes excelsa
plants.context: Doryanthes excelsa [Section 8], or Gymea Lily, is found only in coastal areas near Sydney, New South Wales.

plants.name: Telopea 'Canberry Gem'
plants.context: Telopea ‘Canberry Gem’ [Section 30], also on your left, forms another spectacular display.

plants.name: Telopea mongaensis
plants.context: Close by on your left is another waratah Telopea mongaensis [Section 30], a smaller bush with deeper red flowers, commonly known as the Monga Waratah or Braidwood Waratah.

plants.name: Pultenaea villosa
plants.context: Turn back now and veer right to see Pultenaea villosa [Section 30] on your right.

plants.name: Bauera rubioides
plants.context: Also on your right is Bauera rubioides [Section 8], or Dog Rose, a large bush with bright pink flowers en masse.The species is widespread throughout coastal and in moist mountain areas in New South Wales, Victoria and Tasmania.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: We will walk to the Rock Garden today, as there are many choice plants in flower there.

plants.name: Doryanthes palmeri
plants.context: On your left as you turn right is Doryanthes palmeri [Section 114] or Giant Spear Lily.

plants.name: Doryanthes excelsa
plants.context: Enter the Rock Garden up the steps to see on your right Doryanthes excelsa, or Gymea Lily [Section 15d].

plants.name: Hibbertia pedunculata
plants.context: Also on your right in a pot is Hibbertia pedunculata [Section 15d], with bright yellow flowers on fine creeping foliage.

plants.name: Grevillea 'Poorinda Royal Mantle'

plants.context: As you continue up the hill on your left is Leptospermum variabile [Section 15c], a large shrub with many branches, small leaves and numerous white ‘tea-tree’ flowers.

plants.name: Eremaea pauciflora var. pauciflora
plants.context: Look to your left to see Eremaea pauciflora var. pauciflora [Section 15b], a small sprawling shrub with orange flowers.

plants.name: Viola hederacea
plants.context: Notice on your left Viola hederacea [Section 15a], a small mauve and white violet on a close groundcover.

plants.context: Also on the right is Labichea lanceolata subsp. lanceolata [Section 15r], a large bush with bright green foliage and yellow flowers with a red throat.

plants.name: Darwinia oxylepis
plants.context: Also on your right in a pot is Darwinia oxylepis [Section 15r], with dainty green foliage and pink bell-flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: A walk along the Main Path this time of the year is a rewarding experience. Flowers are plentiful from the moment you leave the Visitor Information Centre (VIC).

plants.name: Pandorea jasminoides

plants.context: Actinotus helianthi ‘Starbright’ [Section 221], or Flannel Flower, is in a pot on the right as you leave the VIC.

plants.name: Pelargonium rodneyanum
plants.context: Low on the right is the groundcover Pelargonium rodneyanum [Section 174], or Magenta Storksbill, with small bright pink/purple flowers on green lobed ‘geranium’ leaves.

plants.name: Melaleuca linariifolia 'Seafoam'
plants.context: Detour across the lawn from the café to see the outstanding small tree Melaleuca linariifolia ‘Seafoam’ [Section 243].

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Today we will walk up the hill behind the café, along the road behind the Rock Garden and finish on the Main Path.

plants.name: Grevillea rosmarinifolia 'Scarlet Sprite'
plants.context: Grevillea rosmarinifolia ‘Scarlet Sprite’ [Section 174] on your right is just coming into bloom with bright red clusters of flowers on a neat bush of fine green foliage.

plants.name: Alyogyne huegelii 'West Coast Gem'
plants.context: On your left up high is Alyogyne huegelii ‘West Coast Gem’ [Section 210] with clear purple ‘hibiscus’ style flowers which open for a short period only but are prolific.

plants.name: Leucopogon attenuatus
plants.context: Leucopogon attenuatus [Section 174] is on your right in a pot with white fluffy flowers on sparse stems.

plants.name: Epacris impressa
plants.context: Epacris impressa [Section 174].

plants.name: Grevillea rosmarinifolia 'Rosy Posy'
plants.context: Grevillea rosmarinifolia ‘Rosy Posy’ [Section 128], on your right, is a compact bush with linear foliage and pendent racemes of pink and cream flowers.

plants.name: Acmena smithii
plants.context: Acmena smithii [Section 140] up the hill on your left is a small tree with a dense crown of shiny green leaves covered in clusters of pink berries.

plants.name: Chamelaucium 'Cascade Brook'
plants.context: Chamelaucium ‘Cascade Brook’ [Section 17], or Geraldton Wax, is on your right - an open airy bush with masses of purplish-pink 5 petalled flowers with darker centres.

plants.name: Hakea obtusa
plants.context: Hakea obtusa [Section 20] further along the road still on your right, is a small tree with grey-green leathery foliage and dark pink powderpuff flowers along the branches.

plants.name: Grevillea tripartita subsp. macrostylis
plants.context: Grevillea tripartita subsp. macrostylis [Section 22], on the right , is an open, rangy plant with dark green, prickly, three lobed foliage and large single red and cream flowers with long showy red styles.

plants.name: Grevillea vestita
plants.context: Grevillea vestita [Section 22], also on the right, is a large open bush with many starbursts of white flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea centrastigma
plants.context: Grevillea centrastigma [Section 26], on your left, is a small bush with soft lush foliage fringed with with white hairs.

plants.name: Adenanthos × cunninghamii
plants.context: Adenanthos x cunninghamii [Section 24], on your right is a small bush with soft swirling silver foliage.

plants.name: Isopogon asper
plants.context: Isopogon asper [Section 26], on your left, is a shrub that is endemic to the southwest botanical province of WA, and first described by botanist Robert Brown in 1830.

plants.name: Grevillea wilsonii × tripartita
plants.context: Grevillea wilsonii x tripartita [Section 26], on your right, is a tall, rangy bush with green prickly foliage and large pink/red spider flowers with red styles.

plants.name: Grevillea trifida
plants.context: Finally on your left is Grevillea trifida [Section 26] with grey-green three-part foliage and cream spider flowers with reddish buds.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Today we will walk around the environs of the café then up the hill towards the Rock Garden.

plants.name: Correa baeuerlenii
plants.context: Turn left as you leave the café to see on your left Correa baeuerlenii [Section 131] with long green bell flowers and shiny foliage.

plants.name: Banksia 'Stumpy Gold'
plants.context: Also on your left is Banksia ‘Stumpy Gold’ [Section 131] with fine, toothed linear foliage and masses of short gold cones with rusty red styles.

plants.name: Dracophyllum macranthum
plants.context: Bear right down the path to see on your right in a pot Dracophyllum macranthum [Section 240], with upright stems of pointed green foliage and dark pink tubular flowers with white tips.

plants.name: Crowea exalata 'Southern Stars'
plants.context: On your left is Crowea exalata ‘Southern Stars’ [Section 240], a dainty bush with dark green foliage and pink star flowers.

plants.name: Crowea saligna 'Rosy Glow'
plants.context: Still on your left is Crowea saligna ‘Rosy Glow’ [Section 240], a small neat bush of green foliage with large pink star flowers.

plants.name: Crowea 'Cooper's Hybrid'
plants.context: To the rear on your left is Crowea ‘Cooper’s Hybrid’ [Section 240], a lax bush with dark green foliage and darker pink star flowers.Crowea 'Cooper's Hybrid' is a cross between C.

plants.name: Pomaderris obcordata
plants.context: Pomaderris obcordata [Section 240] is also on your left, a small bush with tiny green leaves and small clusters of pink flowers.

plants.name: Corymbia ficifolia 'Dwarf Orange'
plants.context: On your right is Corymbia ficifolia ‘Dwarf Orange’ [Section 240], a small tree with green foliage, pink stems and magnificent nuts.

plants.name: Grevillea rosmarinifolia 'Scarlet Sprite'
plants.context: Behind the Corymbia, also on your right, is Grevillea rosmarinifolia ‘Scarlet Sprite’ [Section 240], just coming into bloom with bright red clusters of flowers on a neat bush of fine green foliage.

plants.name: Acacia alata var. biglandulosa
plants.context: Turn left up the hill, then up the steps to see on your left Acacia alata var. biglandulosa [Section 240], or Winged Wattle, with flattened phyllodes and masses of white fluffy balls of flowers.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa var. collina
plants.context: Continue up the hill to see Banksia spinulosa var. collina [Section 27] on your left, with fine linear foliage and slender, dull gold cones.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa var. spinulosa
plants.context: Further on your left is Banksia spinulosa var. spinulosa [Section 109], or Hairpin Banksia, which is found in open forests and woodlands of the coasts and mountains of New South Wales and Queensland.

plants.name: Grevillea aspleniifolia
plants.context: Further up the hill on your left is Grevillea aspleniifolia [Section 124], a very large sprawling shrub with long linear toothed green foliage and pink “toothbrush” flowers.

plants.name: Correa alba
plants.context: Also on your left is Correa alba [Section 124], with grey-green leaves and white star flowers.

plants.name: Geijera parviflora
plants.context: On your right is Geijera parviflora [Section 4], or Wilga, a small tree with attractive linear green leaves which are aromatic when crushed.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Today we will walk from the Visitor Information Centre (VIC) up the hill behind the café in search of early-flowering wattles.

plants.name: Crowea exalata
plants.context: Crowea exalata [Section 221], on your right in a pot as you leave the VIC, forms a mounded bush of fine green foliage with red stems dotted with pink star flowers.

plants.name: Leucopogon attenuatus
plants.context: Leucopogon attenuatus [Section 174] is further on your right in a pot.

plants.name: Acronychia littoralis
plants.context: Bear left up the road behind the café to see on your left Acronychia littoralis [Section 114].

plants.name: Acacia amoena
plants.context: Bear right along the road behind the Rock Garden to see Acacia amoena [Section 3], or Boomerang Wattle, on your left.

plants.name: Acacia blayana
plants.context: Acacia blayana [Section 2] is on your left, with grey-green foliage and bright yellow balls of flowers.

plants.name: Acacia 'Purpurea'
plants.context: Acacia 'Purpurea' [Section 3] on your left has many sprays of golden balls of flowers with striking silver-grey fringed foliage with a feathery texture.

plants.name: Acacia boormanii
plants.context: Acacia boormanii [Section 3], or Snowy River Wattle, on your left, has fine needle foliage and masses of golden balls of flowers.

plants.name: Acacia ulicifolia
plants.context: Turn left up the hill to see Acacia ulicifolia [Section 18], or Prickly Moses, on your right, with many pale yellow balls of flowers on fine, dark green, prickly foliage.

plants.name: Acacia oshanesii
plants.context: On your left is Acacia oshanesii [Section 3], native to coastal New South Wales and Queensland.

plants.name: Acacia decora
plants.context: Acacia decora [Section 1], or Showy Wattle, on your left, has grey-green foliage and large golden balls of flowers.

plants.name: Acacia caesiella
plants.context: Turn left along the edge of the Eucalypt Lawn to see on your left Acacia caesiella [Section 1], from the central slopes of New South Wales.

plants.name: Acacia cardiophylla
plants.context: Turn back across the path to your right to see on your right Acacia cardiophylla [Section 18], or West Wyalong Wattle, with ferny light green bipinnate foliage and masses of yellow balls of flowers.

plants.name: Acacia trigonophylla
plants.context: Continue over to the main path leading downhill to see Acacia trigonophylla [Section 18] on your far left, which is an interesting wattle with flattened phyllodes and gold balls of flowers blooming on the stem.

plants.name: Acacia consobrina
plants.context: On both your left and right is Acacia consobrina [Section 18], native to southwestern Western Australia.

plants.name: Acacia venulosa
plants.context: Acacia venulosa [Section 18], further along on your left, has green linear foliage and bright yellow balls of flowers.

title: In Flower This Week - Australian National Botanic Gardens
intro: Today we will walk from the Visitor Information Centre (VIC) up the Main Path to see the winterflowering grevilleas.

plants.name: Homoranthus thomasii
plants.context: Look left as you leave the VIC to see in a pot Homoranthus thomasii [Section 221], a small bush with grey-green leaves, dark red stems and tiny red bell flowers with white tips.

plants.name: Acacia baileyana (prostrate form)
plants.context: Go across the bridge, past the café and up the hill on the Main Path to see on your left Acacia baileyana (prostrate form) [Section 30], or Cootamundra Wattle, with bright gold balls of flower on drooping greygreen fringed foliage.

plants.name: Homoranthus flavescens
plants.context: Further on your right is Homoranthus flavescens [Section 30], with acid yellow blooms layered on a small neat bush.

plants.name: Grevillea acropogon
plants.context: Low on your right is Grevillea acropogon [Section 30], a low bush with green foliage and deep red clusters of flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea saccata
plants.context: Grevillea saccata [Section 30], in a pot on your right, has weeping branches with bright green upright leaves and pinkish-orange flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea sericea subsp. sericea
plants.context: Grevillea sericea subsp. sericea [Section 27], on your right, is an airy bush with light green foliage and white spider flowers.

plants.name: Grevillea 'LadyO'
plants.context: Grevillea 'LadyO' [Sections 24 and 26], across the road on the left and right, is a long-blooming shrub with red flowers and bright green foliage.

plants.name: Hakea 'Winter Burgundy'
plants.context: On your right is Hakea 'Winter Burgundy' [Section 26], a tall upright bush with greygreen leaves and bright burgundy blooms.

plants.name: Grevillea lavandulacea
plants.context: Grevillea lavandulacea [Section 26], also on your right, commonly known as Lavender Grevillea, is found in southeastern South Australia and western and central Victoria.

plants.name: Grevillea speciosa
plants.context: Grevillea speciosa [Section 26], on your right, also known as Red Spider Flower, is a shrub which is endemic to New South Wales.

plants.name: Grevillea manglesii subsp. manglesii
plants.context: Grevillea manglesii subsp. manglesii [Section 24], or Birdsfoot Grevillea, on your left is a large open bush with white "pincushion" flower heads all along the stems.

plants.name: Grevillea wilsonii × tripartita
plants.context: Grevillea wilsonii × tripartita [Section 24], is on your left, a tall, rangy bush with prickly green foliage and large red and cream spider flowers with red styles.

plants.name: Grevillea tripartita subsp. macrostylis
plants.context: Grevillea tripartita subsp. macrostylis [Section 24], on the left, is an open, rangy plant with dark green, prickly, three-lobed foliage and large single pink and cream flowers with long showy red styles.

plants.name: Grevillea ripicola
plants.context: Grevillea ripicola [Section 24], on the left, commonly known as Collie Grevillea, is a shrub endemic to south-west Western Australia.

plants.name: Grevillea centristigma
plants.context: Grevillea centristigma [Section 26], on your right, is a small bush with soft lush green foliage fringed with white hairs.
